essay.en: The surah opens abruptly, its first word a declaration of repudiation (bara'a) from Allah and His Apostle toward the polytheists with whom the Muslims held standing treaties. Tabatabai reads this as a judgment lifting the polytheists' guarantee of safety, not an arbitrary breaking of the treaty without a cause that permits it [1]. The polytheists are granted four months to travel the land unhindered and see to their affairs, safe from the sword [2]; after that they can neither frustrate Allah nor escape His disgrace. Verse three then carries a public proclamation, on the day of the greater Hajj, that Allah and His Apostle are quit of the polytheists, and it leaves a door open: to repent is better for them [3]. An exception is spared for those who had kept every term of their treaty and backed no enemy against the Muslims - their treaty is to be fulfilled to its end [8]. When the sacred months pass, the polytheists are to be fought, seized and besieged; yet if they repent and maintain the prayer and give the zakat, they are let go. Tusi notes that this verse grounds the ruling that one who deliberately abandons the prayer may be killed [9]. The passage closes in restraint: any polytheist who seeks asylum is to be granted it until he hears the Word of Allah, and then escorted to his place of safety [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و كانت سيرة رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) قبل نزول سورة براءة أن لا يقاتل إلا من قاتله، و لا يحارب إلا من حاربه و أراده … حتى نزلت عليه سورة براءة، و أمره الله بقتل المشركين من اعتزله و من لم يعتزله، إلا الذين قد عاهدهم رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) يوم فتح مكة إلى مدة
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Before Surat Bara'a came down, the Messenger of Allah fought only those who fought him and warred only on those who warred on him. Then Bara'a was revealed, and Allah commanded him to fight the polytheists, whether they had withdrawn from him or not, except those he had treatied with at Mecca's conquest for a fixed term.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: الآذان أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام وفي حديث آخر قال: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام كنت أنا الآذان في الناس وقوله: { يوم الحج الأكبر } قال: هو يوم النحر
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: 'The announcement (adhan)' is Amir al-Mu'minin; and in another report he said: Amir al-Mu'minin said, I myself was the announcement among the people. And 'the day of the greater Hajj' is the day of sacrifice.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: اسم نحله الله عز وجل عليا صلوات الله عليه من السماء لأنه هو الذي أدى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله براءة وقد كان بعث بها مع أبي بكر أولا فنزل عليه جبرئيل عليه السلام فقال: يا محمد إن الله يقول لك: إنه لا يبلغ عنك إلا أنت أو رجل منك
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is a name Allah bestowed on Ali from heaven, because it was he who delivered Bara'a on behalf of the Messenger of Allah. It had first been sent with Abu Bakr; then Jibril came down and said: O Muhammad, Allah tells you that none shall deliver on your behalf but you or a man from you.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أن رجلا قال لعلي بن أبي طالب (عليه السلام): فمن أراد منا أن يلقى رسول الله في بعض الأمر بعد انقضاء الأربعة، فليس له عهد؟ قال علي (عليه السلام): بلى، إن الله تعالى قال: { وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ الآية
narrations.chain: Ibn Shahr Ashub, from Tafsir al-Qushayri

text.en: A man asked Ali: after the four months have passed, has one of us who wishes to come to the Messenger of Allah on some matter no protection? Ali said: Yes, he has - for Allah has said, 'If any of the polytheists seeks asylum from you, grant him asylum.'

perspectives.en: Verse 3 sets the proclamation on 'the day of the greater Hajj,' and commentators dispute which day is meant. Shia narrations from the Imams fix it as the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr): al-Sadiq reports that Amir al-Mu'minin argued from the four-month count that it cannot fall on the day of Arafah [50]. Among Sunnis the matter is split: al-Tabari records many authorities, Umar among them, holding that it is the day of Arafah [23], while Qurtubi notes that Ali, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud named the day of sacrifice, which al-Tabari himself preferred [34].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالمراد بالآية القضاء برفع الأمان عن الذين عاهدوهم من المشركين وليس رفعاً جزافياً وإبطالاً للعهد من غير سبب يبيح ذلك

sources.gloss: What the verse intends is the judgment lifting the guarantee of safety from those polytheists they had treaties with - not an arbitrary lifting, nor an annulment of the treaty without a cause that permits it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { فسيحوا في الأرض } أي سيروا في الأرض على وجه المهل وتصرَّفوا في حوائجكم آمنين من السيف

sources.gloss: 'Travel in the land' means go about the land unhurried and see to your needs, safe from the sword.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { وأذان من الله ورسوله إلى الناس } معناه وإعلام وفيه معنى الأمر أي أذنوا الناس

sources.gloss: 'And an announcement from Allah and His Apostle to the people' means a proclamation, carrying a command: proclaim to the people.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فهؤلاء إن لم يعاونوا عليكم احداً من اعدائكم ولا نقصوكم شيئاً من حقكم في عهدهم فأتموا اليهم عهدهم إلى مدتهم

sources.gloss: So these, if they aided none of your enemies against you and diminished nothing of your right under their treaty, then fulfill their treaty to its term.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واستدل بهذه الاية على ان تارك الصلاة متعمداً يجب قتله

sources.gloss: This verse is cited as proof that one who deliberately abandons the prayer must be killed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ان استأمنك احد فأمنه { حتى يسمع كلام الله }

sources.gloss: If someone seeks your protection, grant it to him until he hears the word of Allah.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال: الآذان أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام وفي حديث آخر قال: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام كنت أنا الآذان في الناس

sources.gloss: He said: 'the announcement' is Amir al-Mu'minin; and in another report Amir al-Mu'minin said, I myself was the announcement among the people.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و أمره الله بقتل المشركين من اعتزله و من لم يعتزله، إلا الذين قد عاهدهم رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) يوم فتح مكة إلى مدة

sources.gloss: Allah commanded him to fight the polytheists, whether they withdrew from him or not, except those the Messenger of Allah had treatied with at the conquest of Mecca for a fixed term.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال علي (عليه السلام): بلى، إن الله تعالى قال: { وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ الآية

sources.gloss: Ali said: Yes, he has - for Allah has said, 'If any of the polytheists seeks asylum from you, grant him asylum.'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: قال عمر رضي الله عنه: يوم الحجّ الأكبرّ: يوم عرفة

sources.gloss: Umar said: the day of the greater Hajj is the day of Arafah.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وعن عليّ وابن عباس أيضاً وابن مسعود وٱبن أبي أَوْفَى والمُغيِرة بن شعبة أنه يوم النَّحر. واختاره الطبري

sources.gloss: From Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, Ibn Abi Awfa and al-Mughira ibn Shuba: it is the day of sacrifice; and al-Tabari preferred this.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: الحج الأكبر يوم النحر واحتج بقول الله عز وجل

sources.gloss: Amir al-Mu'minin said: the greater Hajj is the day of sacrifice, and he argued from the word of Allah (the four months of travel).

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: اسم نحله الله عز وجل عليا صلوات الله عليه من السماء لأنه هو الذي أدى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله براءة

sources.gloss: It is a name Allah bestowed on Ali from heaven, because it was he who delivered Bara'a on behalf of the Messenger of Allah.

essay.en:
The passage opens with a question whose answer is 'none': how can the idolaters hold a valid treaty with Allah and His Messenger while they hide treachery? Tabatabai stresses that the earlier renunciation was not an arbitrary tearing-up of pledges but a response in kind to oaths the idolaters had already broken [1], and Tabrisi reads the 'how' as astonishment or denial [2]. The one exception is those who kept their treaty at the Holy Mosque: 'so long as they are steadfast with you, be steadfast with them.' Commentators dispute who these were - Khuza'a, Banu Kinana, or Quraysh [6] - and Tabrisi holds closest the view naming tribes of Bakr who had not broken their pledge, since the verses came down after Quraysh broke faith and after the conquest of Mecca [2].

Verse 8 repeats the question: were these idolaters to gain the upper hand, they would honour neither kinship nor covenant, pleasing with their mouths while their hearts refuse [7]. They sold Allah's signs for a paltry gain and turned people from His way [3]; Tusi records a report that this described Abu Sufyan, who fed his own allies and left out the Prophet's [8]. They keep no faith toward a believer, and the verse presses the Muslims to fight them [9]. Yet the door stays open: if they repent, keep the prayer and pay the zakat, they are brethren in faith [10].

Then the ruling: fight the leaders of unfaith. Verse 13 urges war on a people who broke their oaths, resolved to expel the Messenger, and opened hostilities first [12]. Verse 14 promises that Allah will punish them by the believers' hands and heal the hearts of a faithful folk - those of Khuza'a, the Prophet's allies, in the reading Tabrisi cites [4]. The passage closes by warning that none is left untested until Allah makes plain who wages jihad and takes no confidant besides Him, His Messenger, and the faithful [5].

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: والله ما قاتلت هذه الفئة الناكثة إلا بآية من كتاب الله عز وجل

text.en: By Allah, I did not fight this treaty-breaking faction except by a verse from the Book of Allah.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: دخل علي أناس من أهل البصرة فسألوني عن طلحة و الزبير، فقلت لهم: كانا من أئمة الكفر
narrations.chain: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid and Abd al-Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hannan ibn Sadir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Some people of Basra came in to me and asked about Talha and Zubair. I told them: they were among the leaders of unbelief.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن بقيتم حتى تروا ما تمدون إليه رقابكم، شفى الله صدوركم، و أذهب غيظ قلوبكم و أدالكم على عدوكم، و هو قول الله تعالى ذكره: { وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُّؤْمِنِينَ * وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ }
narrations.chain: al-Barqi, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba ibn Khalid

text.en: If you remain until you see that toward which you stretch your necks, Allah will heal your breasts, remove the rage of your hearts, and give you the upper hand over your enemy - that is Allah's word: 'and heal the hearts of a faithful folk, and remove rage from their hearts.'

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم، فإن لم تفعلوا ليعذبنهم الله بأيدي غيركم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Ja'd, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih, from Shu'ayb ibn Rashid, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands; and if you do not, Allah will surely punish them by the hands of others.

note.en: A walija is an outsider brought into a group, a confidant one lets into one's private affairs; anything drawn into something it does not belong to is a walija [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يَعْنِي بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ الائِمَّةَ (عليهم السلم) لَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا الْوَلائِجَ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from al-Muthanna, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: By 'the faithful' the Imams are meant; they took no confidants besides them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Hasan al-Askari
narrations.arabic: الوليجة: الذي يقام دون ولي الأمر … فهم الأئمة الذين يؤمنون على الله فيجيز أمانهم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Nakha'i, from Sufyan ibn Muhammad al-Dab'i

text.en: The walija is the one set up in place of the master of the affair. The believers here are the Imams, who grant protection on Allah's behalf, and He allows the protection they give.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kadhim
narrations.arabic: أما والله، لا يكون الذي تمدون إليه أعينكم حتى تميزوا أو تمحصوا، حتى لا يبقى منكم إلا الأندر
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr

text.en: By Allah, that toward which you strain your eyes will not come until you are set apart and sifted, until none of you remains but the fewest.

perspectives.en: On 'fight the leaders of unfaith,' the two traditions aim the verse at different targets. Shia narrations turn it on the People of the Camel: al-Sadiq named Talha and Zubair among the leaders of unbelief [17], and the Qummi report says it came down about them [15]. Tabari identifies the leaders as chiefs of Quraysh - Abu Jahl, Utba, Abu Sufyan and their like [30] - and Ibn Kathir holds the verse general, even if its occasion was Quraysh [38]. On verse 16, the Imams read 'the faithful' as themselves [65], while Tabari reads walija as a confidant taken from among the polytheists [34].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالمراد بالآية القضاء برفع الأمان عن الذين عاهدوهم من المشركين وليس رفعاً جزافياً وإبطالاً للعهد من غير سبب يبيح ذلك

sources.gloss: What the verse means is the ruling to lift the security of those idolaters with whom a treaty was made, and this is not an arbitrary lifting or an annulment of the pact without a cause that permits it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذا يكون على التعجب أو على الجحد … وهذا القول أقرب إلى الصواب لأن هذه الآيات نزلت بعد نقض قريش العهد وبعد فتح مكة

sources.gloss: This is by way of astonishment or denial ... and this view is closest to correct, because these verses came down after Quraysh broke the treaty and after the conquest of Mecca.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ومعناه أعرضوا عن دين الله وصدُّوا الناس عنه بشيء يسير نالوه من الدنيا

sources.gloss: It means: they turned away from Allah's religion and turned people from it for something trifling they gained of this world.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعني صدور بني خزاعة الذين بيَّت عليهم بنو بكر عن مجاهد والسدي لأنهم كانوا حلفاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: Meaning the breasts of Banu Khuza'a, whom Banu Bakr fell upon by night, per Mujahid and al-Suddi, for they were the Prophet's allies.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: معناه أظننتم أيها المؤمنون أن تتركوا من دون أن تكلّفوا الجهاد في سبيل الله مع الإخلاص

sources.gloss: It means: do you suppose, O believers, that you will be left off without being charged with jihad in the way of Allah, with sincerity?

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قيل فيهم ثلاثة اقوال: قال مجاهد: هم خزاعة. وقال ابن اسحاق: هم قوم من بني كنانة. وقال ابن عباس: هم قريش

sources.gloss: Three views are given about them: Mujahid said they are Khuza'a; Ibn Ishaq, a people of Banu Kinana; Ibn Abbas, Quraysh.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يقولون قولا يرضيكم بذلك في الظاهر وتأبى قلوبهم أن يذعنوا لكم

sources.gloss: They say words that please you outwardly, while their hearts refuse to submit to you.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال مجاهد: نزلت في ابي سفيان لما جمعهم على طعامه فاطعم حلفاءه وترك حلفاء النبي صلى الله عليه وآله

sources.gloss: Mujahid said: it was revealed about Abu Sufyan, when he gathered them at his meal and fed his allies and left out the Prophet's allies.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والغرض بالآية حث المسلمين على قتالهم

sources.gloss: The aim of the verse is to urge the Muslims to fight them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فانهم يكونون اخوان المؤمنين في الدين، والايمان

sources.gloss: Then they become the brethren of the believers in religion and faith.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: حض الله تعالى المؤمنين على قتال الكفار الذين نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول من مكة

sources.gloss: Allah urged the believers to fight the unbelievers who broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger from Mecca.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكل شيء دخل في شيء وليس منه فهو وليجة

sources.gloss: Anything that enters into something it is not part of is a walija.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإنها نزلت في أصحاب الجمل وقال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام يوم الجمل والله ما قاتلت هذه الفئة الناكثة إلا بآية من كتاب الله

sources.gloss: It was revealed about the People of the Camel; and Amir al-Muminin said on the day of the Camel: By Allah, I did not fight this treaty-breaking faction except by a verse from the Book of Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فسألوني عن طلحة و الزبير، فقلت لهم: كانا من أئمة الكفر

sources.gloss: They asked me about Talha and Zubair, and I said to them: they were among the leaders of unbelief.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن بقيتم حتى تروا ما تمدون إليه رقابكم، شفى الله صدوركم، و أذهب غيظ قلوبكم

sources.gloss: If you remain until you see that toward which you stretch your necks, Allah will heal your breasts and remove the rage of your hearts.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الوليجة: الذي يقام دون ولي الأمر … فهم الأئمة الذين يؤمنون على الله فيجيز أمانهم

sources.gloss: The walija is the one set up in place of the master of the affair ... they are the Imams who grant protection on Allah's behalf, and He allows their protection.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: هم أبو جهل بن هشام، وعتبة بن ربيعة، وأبو سفيان بن حرب ونظراؤهم

sources.gloss: They are Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Utba ibn Rabi'a, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and their like.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وإنما عنى بها في هذا الموضع: البطانة من المشركين

sources.gloss: What is meant by it here is a confidant from among the polytheists.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والصحيح أن الآية عامة، وإن كان سبب نزولها مشركي قريش فهي عامة لهم ولغيرهم

sources.gloss: The sound view is that the verse is general, and though its occasion was the polytheists of Quraysh, it applies to them and others.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم، فإن لم تفعلوا ليعذبنهم الله بأيدي غيركم

sources.gloss: Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands; and if you do not, Allah will surely punish them by the hands of others.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: يَعْنِي بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ الائِمَّةَ (عليهم السلم) لَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا الْوَلائِجَ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ

sources.gloss: By 'the faithful' are meant the Imams, who did not take confidants besides them.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. al-hasan al-tusi

excerpt.text: لا يكون الذي تمدون إليه أعينكم حتى تميزوا أو تمحصوا، حتى لا يبقى منكم إلا الأندر

sources.gloss: That toward which you strain your eyes will not come until you are set apart and sifted, until none of you remains but the fewest.

essay.en:
The passage turns on one measure: a deed counts before God only when it grows from real faith, and without that faith even the proudest service of the Sanctuary is void [1]. It opens by barring the polytheists from maintaining God's mosques while they testify against themselves by their unbelief; their works have failed and the Fire is their home. Tabrisi reads this as the sequel to the order to fight the polytheists and cut off alliance with them: having severed that tie, God now bars them from the mosques [2]. Al-Qummi ties the ban to a nearer offense - that they had driven the Messenger out of the Mosque itself [13]. Verse 18 names who may maintain them: those who believe in God and the Last Day, keep the prayer, pay the zakat, and fear no one but God. Of such God says they will 'hopefully' be guided, and Tusi reads God's 'hopefully' here as binding, not a matter of doubt [6].

Verses 19 and 20 press the point as a question: is watering the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque the equal of one who believes and wages jihad? They are not equal; those who believed, migrated, and strove with wealth and life hold the greater rank and are the triumphant. Tabrisi records the verse as revealed amid a boast at the Sanctuary: Talha claimed custody of the House and Abbas the watering, while Ali answered that he had prayed toward the qibla six months before others and was the man of jihad [3]. Al-Qummi reads that greater rank as a description of Ali himself [16].

Verses 21 and 22 give that reward: mercy, God's good pleasure, and gardens of lasting bliss forever. Verses 23 and 24 carry the line into the household. Believers are not to take even fathers and brothers as allies if they choose unbelief over faith; Tabrisi limits this to the matter of religion, since in worldly affairs there is no harm in keeping their company [4]. The closing verse sets an ultimatum: if kin, wealth, trade, and homes are dearer than God, His Messenger, and jihad, then wait for God's command. Al-Tibyan records, from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, that verse 23 was revealed about Hatib b. Balta'a, who wrote to Quraysh betraying the Prophet's march on Mecca [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزلت في علي وحمزة والعباس وشيبة قال العباس أنا أفضل لأن سقاية الحاج بيدي وقال شيبة أنا أفضل لأن حجابة البيت وقال حمزة أنا أفضل لأن عمارة البيت بيدي وقال علي: أنا أفضل آمنت قبلكم ثم هاجرت وجاهدت فرضوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله حكماً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: It was revealed about Ali, Hamza, Abbas, and Shayba. Abbas said, 'I am superior, for I water the pilgrims'; Shayba, 'for I hold the custody of the House'; Hamza, 'for I maintain the House'; Ali, 'I am superior; I believed before you, then migrated and fought.' They accepted the Messenger as arbiter, and God sent this down.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: يا علي إن عبدالمطلب سن في الجاهية خمس سنن أجارها الله له في الاسلام … ولما حفر زمزم سماها سقاية الحاج، فأنزل الله أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقَايَةَ الْحَاجِّ وَعِمَارَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ كَمَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ وَجَاهَدَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لاَ يَسْتَوُونَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ لاَ يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah, from Abu Hamid, from Abu Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi, from his father, from Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: O Ali, Abd al-Muttalib set five practices in the age of ignorance which God upheld for him in Islam. When he dug the Zamzam well, he named it the watering of the pilgrims, and so God revealed, 'Do you make the watering of pilgrims and the upkeep of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes...?'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فإن الكفر في الباطن في هذه الآية ولاية الأول و الثاني، و هو كفر. و قوله: { عَلَى ٱلإِيمَانِ } فالإيمان ولاية علي بن أبي طالب
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The unfaith in the inner sense of this verse is allegiance to the first and the second, and that is unfaith. And 'over faith' - the faith here is the wilaya of Ali b. Abi Talib.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: لما أذن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام بمكة أن لا يدخل المسجد الحرام مشرك بعد ذلك العام جزعت قريش جزعاً شديداً وقالوا ذهبت تجارتنا وضاعت عيالنا وخربت دورنا فأنزل الله عزوجل في ذلك

text.en: When the Commander of the Faithful proclaimed at Mecca that no polytheist should enter the Sacred Mosque after that year, Quraysh grieved bitterly and said, 'Our trade is gone, our dependents are lost, our homes are ruined.' So God sent down this verse about that.

perspectives.en: On verse 23 the traditions divide. Shia narrations add an inner sense: al-Baqir reads the 'unfaith' preferred over faith as allegiance to 'the first and the second,' and the 'faith' as the wilaya of Ali [21]. The Sunni commentators carry no such layer; Tabari confines the verse to its plain sense, a ban on taking disbelieving fathers and brothers as intimates to whom one betrays Islam's weak points, and a summons to leave the abode of unbelief for migration [32]. On verse 19, though, both sides converge: Qurtubi too holds that the boast at the Sanctuary vindicated Ali over those who prided themselves on its service [39].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان آيات تبين أن الأعمال إنما تكون حية مرضية إذا صدرت عن حقيقة الإِيمان بالله ورسوله واليوم الآخر وإلا فإنما هي حبط لا تهدي صاحبها إلى سعادة، وإن من لوازم الإِيمان بحقيقته قصر الولاية والحب والوداد في الله ورسوله.

sources.gloss: An exposition of verses showing that deeds are living and pleasing to God only when they issue from the reality of faith in God, His Messenger, and the Last Day; otherwise they are void and do not guide their doer to felicity, and among the requirements of true faith is confining loyalty, love, and affection to God and His Messenger.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لما أمر الله سبحانه بقتال المشركين وقطع العصمة والموالاة عنهم أمر بمنعهم عن المساجد

sources.gloss: When God commanded fighting the polytheists and severing protection and alliance with them, He commanded barring them from the mosques.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وذلك أنهم افتخروا فقال طلحة أنا صاحب البيت وبيدي مفتاحه ولو أشاء بت فيه وقال العباس: أنا صاحب السقاية والقائم عليها. وقال علي ع: ما أدري ما تقولان لقد صلّيت إلى القبلة ستة أشهر قبل الناس، وأنا صاحب الجهاد

sources.gloss: For they boasted: Talha said, 'I am master of the House and its key is in my hand; if I wished I would sleep in it'; Abbas said, 'I am in charge of the watering'; and Ali said, 'I do not know what you two are saying; I prayed toward the qibla six months before the people, and I am the man of jihad.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذا في أمر الدين فأما في أمر الدنيا فلا بأس بمجالستهم ومعاشرتهم

sources.gloss: This prohibition concerns the matter of religion; as for worldly affairs, there is no harm in sitting with and keeping company with them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لان عسى من الله واجبة ليست على طريق الشك

sources.gloss: For 'perhaps' (asa) from God is binding, not by way of doubt.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: روي عن ابي جعفر وابي عبد الله عليهما السلام ان هذه الآية نزلت في حاطب بن بلتعة حيث كتب إلى قريش بخبر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله حين أراد فتح مكة

sources.gloss: It is narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that this verse was revealed about Hatib b. Balta'a, who wrote to Quraysh with news of the Prophet when he intended to conquer Mecca.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي: لا يعمروا وليس لهم أن يقيموا وقد أخرجوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله منه

sources.gloss: That is, they may not maintain them, nor is it theirs to remain, for they have expelled the Messenger of God from it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت في علي وحمزة والعباس وشيبة

sources.gloss: It was revealed about Ali, Hamza, Abbas, and Shayba.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وصف علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام

sources.gloss: He described Ali b. Abi Talib [in the words 'those who believed, migrated, and did jihad... a greater rank near God'].

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لما أذن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام بمكة أن لا يدخل المسجد الحرام مشرك بعد ذلك العام جزعت قريش جزعاً شديداً

sources.gloss: When the Commander of the Faithful proclaimed at Mecca that no polytheist would enter the Sacred Mosque after that year, Quraysh grieved intensely.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فإن الكفر في الباطن في هذه الآية ولاية الأول و الثاني، و هو كفر. و قوله: { عَلَى ٱلإِيمَانِ } فالإيمان ولاية علي بن أبي طالب

sources.gloss: The unfaith in the inner sense of this verse is allegiance to the first and the second, and it is unfaith; and 'over faith' - faith is the wilaya of Ali b. Abi Talib.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم بطانة وأصدقاء تفشون إليهم أسراركم وتطلعونهم على عورة الإسلام وأهله، وتؤثرون المكث بين أظهرهم على الهجرة إلى دار الإسلام

sources.gloss: Do not take your fathers and brothers as intimates and friends to whom you disclose your secrets and reveal the weak points of Islam and its people, preferring to remain among them over migration to the abode of Islam.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: افتخر عَباسٌ بالسقاية، وشِيبَةُ بالعمارة، وعليٌّ بالإسلام والجهاد فصدَّق الله عليّاً وكذبهما

sources.gloss: Abbas boasted of the watering, Shayba of the upkeep, and Ali of Islam and jihad; so God confirmed Ali and belied the other two.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: ولما حفر زمزم سماها سقاية الحاج، فأنزل الله أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقَايَةَ الْحَاجِّ وَعِمَارَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ

sources.gloss: When Abd al-Muttalib dug the Zamzam well, he named it 'the watering of the pilgrims,' and so God revealed, 'Do you make the watering of pilgrims and the upkeep of the Sacred Mosque...'

title.en: Hunayn, the Sacred Mosque, and jizya

essay.en:
These verses first recall the battle of Hunayn, a valley between Mecca and Ta'if where the Prophet fought Hawazin and Thaqif shortly after the conquest of Mecca [1][6]. Allah reminds the believers that He had helped them "in many situations," which Tabatabai reads as a preamble to Hunayn's harder lesson [1]: their great numbers pleased them, availed them nothing, and the earth "became narrow" until they found no place to flee and turned their backs [3][6]. Then Allah "sent down His composure" - the calm that stills fear - upon His Apostle and the faithful, and sent hosts "you did not see," which the commentators identify as angels; the disbelievers were punished with killing and capture [3][7]. Yet the door stays open: Allah "shall turn clemently ... to whomever He wishes," accepting the repentance of those who fled or later entered Islam [8].

The passage then turns to law. Because "the polytheists are indeed unclean," they are barred from the Holy Mosque after year nine of the Hijra, the year Ali proclaimed the immunity [1][4]. Fearing the loss of trade and poverty, the believers are promised that Allah will enrich them from His grace [4][9]. Finally comes the command to fight the People of the Book who reject faith and the true religion until they pay the tribute, degraded [2][5][10]. Tabatabai reads "from among those given the Book" as explanatory, covering Jews, Christians and Magians alike [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الكثير ثمانون فما زاد، لقول الله عز و جل: … و كانت ثمانين موطنا
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning a man who vowed to give much wealth in charity, he said: much is eighty and above, because of Allah's words, 'Allah has certainly helped you in many situations' - and they were eighty places.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وقال رجل من بني نضر بن معاوية يقال له شجرة بن ربيعة للمؤمنين وهو أسير في أيديهم أين الخيل البلق والرجال عليهم الثياب البيض؟ فإنما كان قتلنا بأيديهم وما كنا نريكم فيهم إلا كهيئة الشامة قالوا تلك الملائكة
narrations.chain: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: A captive in the believers' hands, Shajara ibn Rabia of Banu Nasr, asked them: Where are the piebald horses and the men in white garments? They were the ones killing us, and among them we saw you only like a small mole. They said: Those were the angels.

narrations.speaker: al-Ma'mun
narrations.arabic: انْهَزَمُوا يَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ فَلَمْ يَبْقَ مَعَ النَّبِيِ‏ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ إِلا سَبْعَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ عَلِيٌ‏ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَضْرِبُ بِسَيْفِهِ وَالْعَبَّاسُ أَخَذَ بِلِجَامِ بَغْلَةِ النَّبِيِ‏ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَالْخَمْسَةُ مُحْدِقُونَ بِالنَّبِيِ‏ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ خَوْفاً مِنْ أَنْ يَنَالَهُ سِلاحُ الْكُفَّارِ حَتَّى أَعْطَى اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى رَسُولَهُ‏ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ الظَّفَرَ عَنَى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي هَذَا الْمَوْضِعِ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وَمَنْ حَضَرَ مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ
narrations.chain: al-Saduq, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Ashari, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad al-Razi, from Ishaq ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from Yahya ibn Aktham

text.en: The people fled on the day of Hunayn, and none remained with the Prophet but seven of Bani Hashim: Ali striking with his sword, and the rest guarding him, until Allah granted His Messenger victory. By 'the believers' here He meant Ali and the Hashimites present.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: لتمنعن مساجدكم يهودكم و نصاراكم و صبيانكم و مجانينكم أو ليمسخنكم الله قردة و خنازير ركعا و سجدا، و قد قال الله عز و جل: { إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلاَ يَقْرَبُواْ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ ٱلْحَرَامَ }
narrations.chain: Da'aim al-Islam, from Ali

text.en: You shall surely keep your Jews, your Christians, your children and your insane from your mosques, or Allah will turn you into apes and swine, bowing and prostrating. Allah has said: 'The polytheists are indeed unclean, so let them not approach the Holy Mosque.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ذاك إلى الإمام أن يأخذ من كل إنسان منهم ما شاء على قدر ماله مما يطيق، إنما هم قوم فدوا أنفسهم من أن يستعبدوا أو يقتلوا … و كيف يكون صاغرا و هو لا يكترث لما يؤخذ منه حتى يجد ذلا لما أخذ منه فيألم لذلك فيسلم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: That is for the Imam: he takes from each of them what he wills, by what his wealth can bear. They are a people who ransomed themselves from enslavement or killing. How is he degraded if he ignores what is taken? Only when he feels the humiliation and submits.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وَالسَّيْفُ الثَّانِي عَلَى أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ فِي أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ ثُمَّ نَسَخَهَا قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللهِ وَلا بِالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ وَلا يُحَرِّمُونَ ما حَرَّمَ اللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَلا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ الْحَقِّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ حَتَّى يُعْطُوا الْجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ وَهُمْ صاغِرُونَ فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْهُمْ فِي دَارِ الإسْلامِ فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُمْ إِلا الْجِزْيَةُ أَوِ الْقَتْلُ
narrations.chain: al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah, from his father Abu Ja'far

text.en: The second sword is upon the people of protection. Allah said, 'Speak kindly to people' - revealed about them, then abrogated by 'Fight those who do not have faith ... until they pay the tribute, degraded.' Whoever is in the abode of Islam, only the tribute or death is accepted from him.

perspectives.en: The verse calls the polytheists "unclean," and the traditions read this differently. Shia jurists take the apparent sense: their bodies are impure, so a wet handshake with a disbeliever requires washing the hand, and they are barred from the Sacred Mosque [4]. The Sunni majority hold instead that the disbelievers' bodies are pure and that the "uncleanness" lies in their disbelief and idolatry; Ibn Kathir reports that most scholars deny bodily impurity, and al-Razi that the jurists agreed their bodies are clean [27][32].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفيها الآية التي تحرّم على المشركين أن يدخلوا المسجد الحرام بعد عام تسع من الهجرة، وهي العام الذي أذن فيه علي عليه السلام ببراءة

sources.gloss: Among these verses is the one forbidding the polytheists to enter the Sacred Mosque after year nine of the Hijra, the year in which Ali proclaimed the immunity.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والسياق يدل على أن لفظة { من } في قوله { من الذين أوتوا الكتاب } بيانية لا تبعيضية

sources.gloss: The context shows that the 'from' in 'from among those given the Book' is explanatory, not partitive.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثم أنزل الله سكينته } أي رحمته التي تسكن إليها النفس ويزول معها الخوف

sources.gloss: 'Then Allah sent down His composure' means His mercy, by which the soul is stilled and fear departs.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: واختلف في نجاسة الكافر فقال قوم من الفقهاء إن الكافر نجس العين وظاهر الآية يدل على ذلك

sources.gloss: Scholars differed over the impurity of the disbeliever: some jurists held he is impure in himself, and the apparent sense of the verse indicates that.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وصف الذين ذكرهم بأنهم من أهل الكتاب وهم اليهود والنصارى وقال أصحابنا: إن المجوس حكمهم حكم اليهود والنصارى

sources.gloss: He described them as being of the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians; our scholars said the Magians have the same ruling as the Jews and Christians.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وحنين اسم واد بين مكة والطائف في قول قتادة

sources.gloss: Hunayn is the name of a valley between Mecca and Ta'if, according to Qatada.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والمراد بها ها هنا الملائكة

sources.gloss: What is meant here [by the hosts] is the angels.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انه يقبل التوبة من بعد هزيمة من انهزم

sources.gloss: That He accepts the repentance of the one who fled, after his flight.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكانوا خافوا انقطاع المتاجر بمنع المشركين، فقال الله تعالى { وإن خفتم عيلة } يعني فقراً بانقطاعهم، فالله يغنيكم من فضله إن شاء

sources.gloss: They had feared the cutting off of trade through the barring of the polytheists, so Allah says He will enrich them from His grace if He wills.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فالصغار الذل والنكال الذي يصغر قدر صاحبه، صغر يصغر صغاراً، فهو صاغر

sources.gloss: 'Degraded' is the lowliness and humiliation that diminishes a person's standing; he is one brought low.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أين الخيل البلق والرجال عليهم الثياب البيض؟ فإنما كان قتلنا بأيديهم وما كنا نريكم فيهم إلا كهيئة الشامة قالوا تلك الملائكة

sources.gloss: 'Where are the piebald horses and the men in white garments? They were the ones killing us, and among them we saw you only like a small mole.' They said: Those were the angels.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الكثير ثمانون فما زاد، لقول الله عز و جل: … و كانت ثمانين موطنا

sources.gloss: Much is eighty and above ... and they were eighty places.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لتمنعن مساجدكم يهودكم و نصاراكم و صبيانكم و مجانينكم

sources.gloss: You shall surely bar your Jews, Christians, children and insane from your mosques.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و كيف يكون صاغرا و هو لا يكترث لما يؤخذ منه حتى يجد ذلا لما أخذ منه فيألم لذلك فيسلم

sources.gloss: How is he degraded when he does not mind what is taken from him, until he finds humiliation in it, feels its pain, and submits?

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وأما نجاسة بدنه، فالجمهور على أنه ليس بنجس البدن والذات

sources.gloss: As for the impurity of his body, the majority hold that he is not impure in body or essence.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وأما الفقهاء فقد اتفقوا على طهارة أبدانهم

sources.gloss: As for the jurists, they agreed on the purity of their bodies.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: عَنَى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي هَذَا الْمَوْضِعِ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وَمَنْ حَضَرَ مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ

sources.gloss: By 'the believers' in this place He meant Ali and those of Bani Hashim who were present.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: وَالسَّيْفُ الثَّانِي عَلَى أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ فِي أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ ثُمَّ نَسَخَهَا

sources.gloss: The second sword is upon the people of protection: 'Speak kindly to people' was revealed about them, then abrogated.

title.en: God's light and the sacred months

essay.en:
Al-Tabatabai reads this section as a survey of the People of the Book's deviations from the truth, in both belief and deed [1]. It opens with two sayings it refuses to let stand: that Ezra is the son of Allah, and that Christ is the son of Allah. Al-Tusi answers the objection that the Jews denied ever saying the first by noting that the Quran ascribes it to them because some among them did hold it [8], and Tabrisi reads the word rendered 'imitating' as resembling the speech of the faithless before them [3].

Verse 31 broadens the charge: they took their scribes and monks as lords besides Allah. Al-Tusi, following what is narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, explains this lordship as obedience rather than worship, accepting from them what they made lawful and unlawful against Allah's command [9]. Then the People of the Book are said to want to put out the light of Allah with their mouths. Al-Tusi records that the commentators take this light to be the Quran and Islam, while al-Jubbai took it to be the proof and demonstration by which people are guided [10]. Verse 33 answers with a promise that the religion of truth will prevail over every religion, a triumph that Tabrisi and al-Tusi, reporting al-Baqir, place at the rising of the Mahdi from the family of Muhammad [4][11].

The address then turns to the believers. Many scribes and monks devour people's wealth wrongfully, which al-Tusi glosses as taking bribes in judgements [12], and they bar others from Allah's way. Those who hoard gold and silver without spending it face a painful punishment, their hoard heated in the Fire to brand them; Tabrisi cites the Prophet that any wealth whose zakat is paid is no hoard [5]. Finally the months are counted: twelve, of which four are sacred, three consecutive and Rajab alone [6]. Al-Tabatabai reads the close as confirming their sanctity and abolishing the intercalation of the age of ignorance [2], the postponing of a sacred month that the verse calls an increase in unfaith [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أما و الله ما دعوهم إلى عبادة أنفسهم، و لو دعوهم إلى عبادة أنفسهم ما أجابوهم، و لكن أحلوا لهم حراما، و حرموا عليهم حلالا، فعبدوهم من حيث لا يشعرون
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: By Allah, they did not call the people to worship them, and had they called them to that, the people would not have obeyed; rather they made the unlawful lawful for them and the lawful unlawful, so the people worshipped them without realizing it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و الله ما نزل تأويلها بعد، و لا ينزل تأويلها حتى يخرج القائم (عليه السلام)، فإذا خرج القائم (عليه السلام) لم يبق كافر بالله العظيم و لا مشرك بالإمام إلا كره خروجه
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sadabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir

text.en: By Allah, the interpretation of this verse has not yet come, and it will not come until the Qaim rises. When the Qaim rises, no one who disbelieves in Almighty Allah or rejects the Imam will remain but that he hates his rising.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: موسع على شيعتنا أن ينفقوا مما في أيديهم بالمعروف، فإذا قام قائمنا حرم على كل ذي كنز كنزه حتى يأتيه به فيستعين به على عدوه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muadh ibn Kathir

text.en: Our Shia are allowed to spend what is in their hands in kindness. But when our Qaim rises, every hoarder's hoard becomes forbidden to him, until he brings it to the Qaim so that he may use it against his enemy.

narrations.speaker: Abu Dharr
narrations.arabic: بشر أهل الكنوز بكي في الجباه وكي في الجنوب وكي في الظهور أبداً حتى يتردد الحر في أجوافهم

text.en: Give the hoarders tidings of a branding on the foreheads, a branding on the sides, and a branding on the backs, on and on, until the heat courses through their bellies.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: { وقاتلوا المشركين كافة } يقول جميعاً كما يقاتلونكم كافة
narrations.chain: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'Fight all the polytheists' means all of them together, just as they fight you all together.

perspectives.en: On making the true religion prevail over all religions (verse 33), the traditions differ on when. Tabrisi and al-Tusi report al-Baqir that the complete triumph comes only when the Mahdi, the Qaim from the family of Muhammad, rises [4][11]. Among Sunni exegetes, al-Tabari records the view that it happens at the coming of Jesus, when the religions become one [34]; al-Razi lists that view alongside al-Suddi's, that it comes at the emergence of the Mahdi [55]; and al-Qurtubi insists the Mahdi is from the Prophet's own family, not Jesus alone [47].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات تأمر بقتال أهل الكتاب ممن يمكن تبقيته بالجزية وتذكر أُموراً من وجوه انحرافهم عن الحق في الاعتقاد والعمل.

sources.gloss: These verses command fighting the People of the Book who can be spared through the jizya, and they list ways in which those people deviate from the truth in belief and in deed.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان في الآيتين بيان حرمة الأشهر الحرم ذي القعدة وذي الحجة والمحرم ورجب الفرد وتثبيت حرمتها وإلغاء نسيء الجاهلية، وفيها الأمر بقتال المشركين كافة.

sources.gloss: These two verses establish the sanctity of the sacred months - Dhul-Qada, Dhul-Hijja, Muharram, and Rajab standing alone - confirm their inviolability, abolish the intercalation of the age of ignorance, and command fighting all the polytheists.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أصل المضاهاة المشابهة

sources.gloss: The root of mudahat, the word rendered 'imitating', is resemblance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقال أبو جعفر ع: إن ذلك يكون عند خروج المهدي من آل محمد فلا يبقى أحد إلا أقرَّ بمحمد

sources.gloss: Abu Jafar [al-Baqir] said: that will be at the emergence of the Mahdi from the family of Muhammad, when no one will remain who does not acknowledge Muhammad.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: كل مال لم تؤدّ زكاته فهو كنز وإن كان ظاهراً وكل مال أدّيت زكاته فليس بكنز وإن كان مدفوناً في الأرض

sources.gloss: Any wealth whose zakat is not paid is a hoard, even if it is out in the open; and any wealth whose zakat is paid is not a hoard, even if buried in the ground.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أربعة أشهر حرم ثلاثة منها سرد ذو القعدة وذو الحجة والمحرم وواحد فرد وهو رجب

sources.gloss: Four sacred months: three in a row, Dhul-Qada, Dhul-Hijja, and Muharram, and one standing alone, Rajab.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر } يعني تأخير الأشهر الحرم عما رتَّبها الله سبحانه عليه

sources.gloss: 'Nasi is an increase in unfaith' means postponing the sacred months out of the order in which Allah arranged them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: إنما اخبر الله بذلك عنهم، لأن منهم من كان يذهب اليه

sources.gloss: Allah reported this saying of them only because some among them did hold that view.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أن معنى اتخاذهم أرباباً أنهم قبلوا منهم التحريم والتحليل بخلاف ما أمر الله تعالى، وهو المروي عن ابي جعفر وابي عبد الله عليهما السلام

sources.gloss: Taking them as lords means they accepted from them the forbidding and permitting that ran contrary to Allah's command; this is narrated from Abu Jafar [al-Baqir] and Abu Abdillah [al-Sadiq].

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: و { نور الله } القرآن والاسلام، في قول المفسرين: السدي والحسن. وقال الجبائي: نور الله: الدلالة والبرهان

sources.gloss: 'The light of Allah' is the Quran and Islam, in the view of the commentators al-Suddi and al-Hasan; and al-Jubbai said the light of Allah is the proof and the demonstration.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال ابو جعفر عليه السلام ان ذلك يكون عند خروج القائم عليه السلام

sources.gloss: Abu Jafar [al-Baqir] said: that will be at the emergence of the Qaim.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل من حيث كانوا يأخذون الرشا في الاحكام

sources.gloss: They devour people's wealth wrongfully, in that they used to take bribes in their judgements.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: بشر أهل الكنوز بكي في الجباه وكي في الجنوب وكي في الظهور أبداً حتى يتردد الحر في أجوافهم

sources.gloss: Give the hoarders tidings of a branding on the foreheads, a branding on the sides, and a branding on the backs, on and on, until the heat courses through their bellies.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { وقاتلوا المشركين كافة } يقول جميعاً كما يقاتلونكم كافة

sources.gloss: 'Fight all the polytheists' - he says, all of them together, just as they fight you all together.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و لكن أحلوا لهم حراما، و حرموا عليهم حلالا، فعبدوهم من حيث لا يشعرون

sources.gloss: But they made the unlawful lawful for them and the lawful unlawful, so the people worshipped them without realizing it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و الله ما نزل تأويلها بعد، و لا ينزل تأويلها حتى يخرج القائم (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: By Allah, its interpretation has not yet come, and it will not come until the Qaim rises.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: موسع على شيعتنا أن ينفقوا مما في أيديهم بالمعروف، فإذا قام قائمنا حرم على كل ذي كنز كنزه حتى يأتيه به فيستعين به على عدوه

sources.gloss: It is allowed for our Shia to spend what is in their hands in kindness; but when our Qaim rises, every hoarder's hoard becomes forbidden to him until he brings it so that it may help against his enemy.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: ذلك عند خروج عيسى حين تصير الملل كلها واحدة

sources.gloss: That is at the coming of Jesus, when all the religions become one.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: أن المهديّ من عِترة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا يجوز حمله على عيسى

sources.gloss: The Mahdi is from the progeny of the Messenger of Allah, so it may not be interpreted as Jesus.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وتمام هذا إنما يحصل عند خروج عيسى، وقال السدي: ذلك عند خروج المهدي

sources.gloss: The completion of this only occurs at the coming of Jesus; and al-Suddi said: that is at the emergence of the Mahdi.

title.en: The call to march for Tabuk

essay.en: These verses open the Quran's rebuke of those who dragged their feet when the Prophet called them to march for the expedition to Tabuk. Al-Tabrisi records that after returning from Ta'if the Prophet ordered the campaign against the Romans, and because it fell at the season of ripening fruit the people found leaving their homes and wealth burdensome [2]. Verse 38 asks what ails believers who, told to go forth in God's way, sink to the ground; al-Tusi notes this can mean clinging to their land or to its harvest [5]. Are they content with this world's fleeting wares over the Hereafter? Verse 39 warns that if they do not march, God will punish them and replace them with another people, and they will not harm Him. Verse 40 turns to the Prophet: even unaided, God already helped him when the disbelievers drove him out, one of two, in the cave, telling his companion not to grieve, sending down His composure and unseen hosts. Al-Tabrisi identifies the cave as Ghar Thawr and the companion as Abu Bakr [3]. Al-Mizan reads the whole section as a rebuke of the believers' sluggishness and the account of the Prophet's flight and the cave [1]. Verse 41 commands them to go forth light and heavy, striving with wealth and selves - which al-Tabrisi takes to mean in every state, easy or hard [4]. Verse 42 exposes those who would have followed a near gain and easy journey but found the distance too far, and who will swear false oaths [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: انفروا- رحمكم الله- إلى قتال عدوكم، و لا تثاقلوا إلى الأرض فتقروا بالخسف، و تبوءوا بالذل و يكون نصيبكم الأخس، و إن أخا الحرب الأرق، و من نام لم ينم عنه

text.en: March - may God have mercy on you - to fight your enemy. Do not sink heavily to the earth, or you will accept humiliation, be saddled with disgrace, and get the meanest share. The brother of war is the wakeful one; whoever sleeps, the enemy does not sleep against him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أقبل يقول لأبي بكر في الغار: اسكن، فإن الله معنا. و قد أخذته الرعدة و هو لا يسكن، فلما رأى رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) حاله، قال: تريد أن أريك أصحابي من الأنصار في مجالسهم يتحدثون، و أريك جعفرا و أصحابه في البحر يغوصون؟ قال: نعم. فمسح رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) بيده على وجهه، فنظر إلى الأنصار في مجالسهم يتحدثون، و نظر إلى جعفر و أصحابه في البحر يغوصون، فأضمر تلك الساعة أنه ساحر
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Yusuf ibn Suhayb, from Abu Abdillah, who said: I heard Abu Jafar say

text.en: In the cave the Messenger of God kept telling Abu Bakr: Be still, God is with us. But trembling seized him. The Prophet said: Shall I show you the Ansar talking in their gatherings, and Ja'far diving in the sea? He said yes. The Prophet wiped his face, he saw them, and then harbored that he was a magician.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) لما خرج من الغار متوجها إلى المدينة، و قد كانت قريش جعلت لمن أخذه مائة من الإبل، فخرج سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم فيمن يطلب، فلحق برسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): اللهم اكفني شر سراقة بما شئت. فساخت قوائم فرسه فثنى رجله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the Messenger of God left the cave for Medina, Quraysh had offered a hundred camels for his capture. Suraqa ibn Malik rode out among the pursuers and caught up with him. The Messenger of God said: O God, guard me against Suraqa's evil as You will. His horse's legs sank into the ground and it threw him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنهم كانوا يستطيعون وقد كان في العلم أنه لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لفعلوا
narrations.chain: His father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, from Sad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thalaba ibn Maymun, from Abd al-Ala ibn Ayun, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: They indeed had the ability, and it was in God's knowledge that had it been a near gain and a short journey, they would have done it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: { لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضاً قَرِيباً } ، يقول: غنيمة قريبة { لاَّتَّبَعُوكَ }
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'Had it been a near gain' means a ready spoil; 'they would have followed you.'

perspectives.en: Verse 40's cave scene divides the traditions. Sunni commentators read it as a distinct merit of Abu Bakr: Ibn Kathir has the Prophet steadying him with 'what do you think of two of whom God is the third?' and names him the Prophet's friend and companion [24], while al-Qurtubi cites Sufyan ibn Uyayna that this verse exempted Abu Bakr from the rebuke of 'If you do not help him' [29]. The Shia narrations instead stress that God's composure descended on His Messenger alone: al-Fayd al-Kashani reports from al-Rida and al-Baqir that the verse mentions the companion with nothing praiseworthy [17]. Both agree the companion is Abu Bakr.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفي مقدّمها عتاب المؤمنين في تثاقلهم عن الجهاد، وحديث خروج النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من مكة وذكر الغار

sources.gloss: At its forefront is the rebuke of the believers for their sluggishness toward jihad, and the account of the Prophet's departure from Mecca and the mention of the cave.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لما رجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الطائف أمر بالجهاد لغزوة الروم وذلك في زمان ادراك الثمار فأحبُّوا المقام في المسكن والمال وشقَّ عليهم الخروج إلى القتال

sources.gloss: When the Messenger returned from Ta'if he ordered jihad for the Roman campaign; that was at the season of ripening fruit, so they loved to stay with home and wealth and found going out to fight burdensome.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والغار الثقب العظيم في الجبل وأراد به هنا غار ثور وهو جبل بمكة … { إذ يقول لصاحبه } أي إذ يقول الرسول لأبي بكر { لا تحزن } أي لا تخف

sources.gloss: The cave is the great hollow in the mountain; here it means Ghar Thawr, a mountain at Mecca. … 'when he said to his companion' means the Messenger said to Abu Bakr 'do not grieve,' that is, do not fear.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والوجه أن يحمل على الجميع فيقال: معناه أخرجوا إلى الجهاد خفّ عليكم أو شقّ على أيّ حالة كنتم

sources.gloss: The sound view is to take it comprehensively: go out to jihad whether it is easy or hard for you, in whatever state you are in.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى { اثاقلتم إلى الأرض } قيل فيه قولان … احدهما - إلى المقام بارضكم ووطنكم … الثاني - لما اخرج من الارض من الثمر والزرع

sources.gloss: 'You sink to the ground' has two explanations: one, clinging to staying in your land and homeland; the other, to what the land yields of fruit and crops.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لو كان المدعو اليه عرضاً قريباً من الغنيمة وما يطمع فيه من المال { وسفراً قاصداً } معناه سفراً سهلا باقتصاده من غير طول في آخره … { ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة } اي بعدت عليهم المسافة، لأنهم دعوا إلى الخروج إلى تبوك ناحية الشام

sources.gloss: Had what they were called to been a near gain and coveted wealth, and an easy journey, they would have followed you; but the distance was too far for them, for they were called to march to Tabuk in the direction of Syria.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: انفروا- رحمكم الله- إلى قتال عدوكم، و لا تثاقلوا إلى الأرض فتقروا بالخسف

sources.gloss: March - may God have mercy on you - to fight your enemy, and do not sink heavily to the earth lest you settle for humiliation.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أقبل يقول لأبي بكر في الغار: اسكن، فإن الله معنا. و قد أخذته الرعدة و هو لا يسكن

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God kept telling Abu Bakr in the cave: Be still, God is with us; but trembling had seized him and he would not settle.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: في رواية أبي الجارود، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، في قوله: { لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضاً قَرِيباً } ، يقول: غنيمة قريبة { لاَّتَّبَعُوكَ }

sources.gloss: In Abu al-Jarud's narration from Abu Jafar on 'had it been a near gain': he said, a ready spoil, 'they would have followed you.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: أنهم كانوا يستطيعون وقد كان في العلم أنه لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لفعلوا

sources.gloss: They indeed had the ability, and it was in God's knowledge that had it been a near gain and short journey they would have done it.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنّهم يحتجون علينا بقول الله تعالى { ثاني اثنين اذ هما في الغار } وما لهم في ذلكَ من حجّة فوالله لقد قال الله فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وما ذكره فيها بخير … فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله قال ألا ترى أنّ السكينة إنّما نزلت على رسوله

sources.gloss: They argue against us with 'the second of two, when the two were in the cave,' but they have no proof in it; by God, God said He sent down His composure upon His Messenger, and did not mention him therein with any good. … God sent His composure upon His Messenger; do you not see that the composure descended only upon His Messenger?

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فخرج منهم هارباً بصحبة صديقه وصاحبه أبي بكر بن أبي قحافة … يا أبا بكر ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما

sources.gloss: So he fled from them in the company of his friend and companion Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa. … O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two of whom God is the third?

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وقال سفيان بن عُيينة: خرج أبو بكر بهذه الآية من المعاتبة التي في قوله: { إِلاَّ تَنصُرُوهُ }

sources.gloss: Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: Abu Bakr was exempted by this verse from the rebuke in 'If you do not help him.'

essay.en:
After rebuking the believers who were slow to march, the surah turns to the hypocrites who schemed to stay home. Tabatabai reads the whole run as an exposure of them, setting out their traits and marks and what Islam and the Muslims suffered from their scheming [1]. It opens with a word to the Prophet, 'May Allah excuse you! Why did you grant them leave,' which Tusi reads not as the sign of a sin but as a reproach for doing what it was better to leave undone [10].

Verses 44 and 45 draw the line: the believer does not seek leave to sit out the struggle on false excuses; it is the doubting, wavering heart that asks [4]. Had these men truly meant to march, they would have made ready; but Allah was averse to their going, for He knew that on the road they would spread slander and act as spies, so their presence would harm more than it helped [5]. Those told to 'be seated with those who sit back' are the women, children, and the disabled [13].

Then comes the man who says, 'Give me leave, and do not put me to temptation.' Tabrisi records that Jadd ibn Qays feared being seduced by the women of Byzantium and asked to stay, while the verse answers that he had already fallen into temptation [6]. The closing verses lay bare their hearts: they grieve when good reaches the Muslims [17], and are told that only one of two excellent outcomes awaits the faithful [19]. Their spending is refused because it flows from rebellion, not faith [7]; neither their wealth nor their children should impress the onlooker [22]; they swear they belong to the believers only from fear of death or capture [8]. It ends with the man who blames the Prophet over the charities, pleased when given and angry when not [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: هذا مما نزل بإياك أعني و اسمعي يا جارة، خاطب الله تعالى بذلك نبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله) و أراد به أمته
narrations.chain: Tamim ibn Abdillah al-Qurashi, from his father, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm

text.en: This belongs to the idiom 'I mean you, but hear it, O neighbour': Allah addressed His Prophet by these words yet intended his community.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: تعرف أهل الغدر والذين جلسوا بغير عذر
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: It means you will recognise the people of treachery and those who sat back without any excuse.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: من تردّد في الريب سبقه الأوّلون وأدركه الآخِرون ووطأته سنابك الشياطين

text.en: Whoever wavers in doubt, those who went before outstrip him, those who come after overtake him, and the hooves of the satans trample him.

note.en: The two excellent things the faithful await are victory by Allah's help or the martyrdom that leads to paradise [19].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إما موت في طاعة الله، أو إدراك ظهور إمام … هو المسخ { أَوْ بِأَيْدِينَا } و هو القتل
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The two good things are either death in obedience to Allah, or living to witness the rising of an Imam. The punishment from Him is transformation; at our hands, it is being killed.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: المرء المسلم البرئ من الخيانة ينتظر احدى الحسنيين إما داعي الله فما عند الله خير له وامّا رزق الله فاذا هو ذو أهل ومال ومعه دينه وحسبه

text.en: The innocent Muslim, free of treachery, awaits one of two good things: either the summoner of Allah, for what is with Allah is better for him, or Allah's provision, so he keeps his family, his wealth, his religion, and his honour.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا يَضُرُّ مَعَ الإيمَانِ عَمَلٌ وَلا يَنْفَعُ مَعَ الْكُفْرِ عَمَلٌ أَ لا تَرَى أَنَّهُ قَالَ وَما مَنَعَهُمْ أَنْ تُقْبَلَ مِنْهُمْ نَفَقاتُهُمْ إِلا أَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِالله وَبِرَسُولِهِ وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ
narrations.chain: from Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Umayya Yusuf ibn Thabit, who heard Abu Abdillah

text.en: With faith, no deed can harm; with disbelief, no deed can benefit. Do you not see He said, 'Nothing prevented their charities from being accepted except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger' - and they died as disbelievers?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُطْمِحَ بَصَرَكَ إِلَى مَنْ فَوْقَكَ فَكَفَى بِمَا قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لِنَبِيِّهِ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وآلِه) فَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ وَقَالَ وَلا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى‏ ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا فَإِنْ دَخَلَكَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ فَاذْكُرْ عَيْشَ رَسُولِ الله (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وآلِه) فَإِنَّمَا كَانَ قُوتُهُ الشَّعِيرَ وَحَلْوَاهُ التَّمْرَ وَوَقُودُهُ السَّعَفَ إِذَا وَجَدَهُ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Hilal

text.en: Never let your eyes reach for one above you. Enough is Allah's word to His Prophet, 'Let not their wealth and children impress you.' If any of that stirs in you, recall the Messenger's life: his food was barley, his sweet dates, his fuel palm twigs when he found them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا إسحاق، كم ترى أهل هذه الآية: { فَإِنْ أُعْطُواْ مِنْهَا رَضُواْ وَإِن لَّمْ يُعْطَوْاْ مِنهَا إِذَا هُمْ يَسْخَطُون … هم أكثر من ثلثي الناس
narrations.chain: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib

text.en: O Ishaq, how many do you think are the people of this verse, 'if they are given from it they are pleased, and if they are not given from it they are displeased'? They are more than two-thirds of mankind.

perspectives.en: The opening of verse 43, 'May Allah excuse you,' divides the traditions. Sunni exegesis generally reads it as a reproof of the Prophet: Tabari says Allah reproved him for granting leave to those he permitted to stay behind [45], though Razi already limits this to leaving the better course, not a sin, since the affair belonged to war and worldly interests [85]. Shia commentators press further to guard the Prophet's infallibility: Tusi calls the words only a reproach for doing what it was better to leave undone, never a fault [10], and Imam al-Rida taught that Allah addressed the Prophet here but meant his community [35].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان تعرّض للمنافقين وفيه بيان لجمل أوصافهم وعلائمهم، وشرح ما لقي الإِسلام والمسلمون من كيدهم ومكرهم وما قاسوه من المصائب من جهة نفاقهم

sources.gloss: An account exposing the hypocrites, setting out their traits and marks, and what Islam and the Muslims suffered from their scheming and deceit.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي لا يطلب منك الإذن في القعود عن الجهاد معك بالمعاذير الفاسدة

sources.gloss: That is, they do not seek permission from you to sit out the jihad with you on false excuses.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ولكن كره الله خروجهم إلى الغزو ولعلمه أنهم لو خرجوا لكانوا يمشون بالنميمة بين المسلمين وكانوا عيوناً للمشركين وكان الضرر في خروجهم أكثر من الفائدة

sources.gloss: Allah was averse to their marching to war, for He knew that had they gone they would spread slander among the Muslims and be spies for the polytheists, and their going would harm more than it helped.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فقام جد بن قيس أخو بني سلمة من بني الخزرج فقال: يا رسول الله ائذن لي ولا تفتنّي ببنات الأصفر فإني أخاف أن أفتتن بهن

sources.gloss: Jadd ibn Qays of Banu Salima stood and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, give me leave and do not tempt me with the Byzantine women, for I fear I will be seduced by them.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإنما لم يتقبل منكم لأنكم كنتم متمرّدين عن طاعة الله والله سبحانه إنما يتقبل من المؤمنين المخلصين

sources.gloss: It was not accepted from you only because you were rebellious against obedience to Allah; He accepts only from sincere believers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي يخافون القتل والأسر إن لم يظهروا الإيمان

sources.gloss: That is, they fear being killed or captured if they do not display faith.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي يعيبك ويطعن عليك في أمر الصدقات

sources.gloss: That is, he finds fault with you and attacks you over the matter of the charities.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قوله { عفا الله عنك } إنما هي كلمة عتاب له صلى الله عليه وآله لم فعل ما كان الأولى به أن لا يفعله

sources.gloss: The words 'Allah has pardoned you' are only a word of reproach to him for doing what it was better for him not to do.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { مع القاعدين } يعني مع النساء والصبيان والمرضى والزمنى، ومن ليس به حراك

sources.gloss: 'With those who sit back' means with the women, the children, the sick, the chronically ill, and those unable to move.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: متى نال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله والمؤمنين حسنة أي نعمة من الله تعالى وظفر باعدائهم وغنيمة ينالونها ساءهم ذلك

sources.gloss: Whenever the Prophet and the believers gain a blessing from Allah, a victory over their enemies or spoils they win, it grieves them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعانيهما ها هنا إما الغلبة بنصر الله عز وجل والشهادة المودية إلى الجنة

sources.gloss: Their meaning here is either victory by Allah's help, or the martyrdom that leads to paradise.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لا يروق ناظركم ايها المؤمنون ظاهر حسنها يعني اموال المنافقين والكفار واولادهم

sources.gloss: O believers, let not the outward beauty of the hypocrites' and disbelievers' wealth and children dazzle your sight.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: تعرف أهل الغدر والذين جلسوا بغير عذر

sources.gloss: It means: you will recognise the people of treachery and those who sat back without excuse.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هذا مما نزل بإياك أعني و اسمعي يا جارة، خاطب الله تعالى بذلك نبيه (صلى الله عليه و آله) و أراد به أمته

sources.gloss: This is of the idiom 'I mean you, but hear it, O neighbour': Allah addressed His Prophet by it but intended his community.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إما موت في طاعة الله، أو إدراك ظهور إمام

sources.gloss: Either death in obedience to Allah, or living to witness the rising of an Imam.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هم أكثر من ثلثي الناس

sources.gloss: They are more than two-thirds of mankind.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: من تردّد في الريب سبقه الأوّلون وأدركه الآخِرون ووطأته سنابك الشياطين

sources.gloss: Whoever wavers in doubt, those who came first outstrip him, those who come last overtake him, and the hooves of the satans trample him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: المرء المسلم البرئ من الخيانة ينتظر احدى الحسنيين إما داعي الله فما عند الله خير له وامّا رزق الله

sources.gloss: The innocent Muslim, free of treachery, awaits one of two good things: either the summoner of Allah, for what is with Allah is better for him, or Allah's provision.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وهذا عتاب من الله تعالى ذكره عاتب به نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم في إذنه لمن أذن له في التخلف عنه

sources.gloss: This is a reproof from Allah, with which He reproved His Prophet for granting leave to those he permitted to stay behind.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: يحمل قوله: { لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ } على ترك الأولى والأكمل، لا سيما وهذه الواقعة كانت من جنس ما يتعلق بالحروب ومصالح الدنيا

sources.gloss: One takes 'Why did you give them leave?' as leaving the better and more complete course, especially since this affair belonged to war and worldly interests.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: لا يَضُرُّ مَعَ الإيمَانِ عَمَلٌ وَلا يَنْفَعُ مَعَ الْكُفْرِ عَمَل

sources.gloss: With faith no deed harms, and with disbelief no deed benefits.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُطْمِحَ بَصَرَكَ إِلَى مَنْ فَوْقَكَ فَكَفَى بِمَا قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لِنَبِيِّهِ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وآلِه) فَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُم

sources.gloss: Never let your eyes reach for one above you; enough for you is Allah's word to His Prophet, 'Let not their wealth and children impress you.'

title.en: The eight shares and the hypocrites

essay.en: The passage opens by settling a complaint the hypocrites had raised about how the Prophet shared out the alms: the obligatory charities belong only to eight named groups - the poor, the needy, the alms-collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, the freeing of slaves, debtors, the way of God, and the traveller - a fixed ordinance from God restricted to these and no others [3]. From here the surah returns to the hypocrites. Some wound the Prophet and sneer that he is an ear who believes whatever he hears; the reply is that he is an ear of good, believing God and trusting the faithful, a mercy to them. They swear by God to please the believers, when God and His Messenger have the better claim to be pleased, and whoever sets himself against God and His Messenger has earned the Fire and the great disgrace. The closing verses catch them exposed: they dread that a surah will lay bare what is in their hearts, and are told to mock on, for God will bring it out. Questioned, they plead they were only chatting and jesting; they are told this was mockery of God, His signs and His Messenger, that excuses are useless, and that they have disbelieved after their profession of faith. Tabatabai holds these verses fit best the plot at the mountain pass on the return from Tabuk [2], the occasion the commentators record [5].

note.en: Here 'the charities' means the obligatory zakat, and the verse restricts it to the eight groups it names and no others [3].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الْفَقِيرُ الَّذِي لاَ يَسْأَلُ النَّاسَ وَالْمِسْكِينُ أَجْهَدُ مِنْهُ وَالْبَائِسُ أَجْهَدُهُمْ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdallah ibn Yahya, from Abdallah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir

text.en: The poor man is the one who does not ask people; the needy is in worse straits than he; and the wretched is the worst off of them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: السَّهْمُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْ ثَمَانِيَةٍ … وَكَذَلِكَ قَسَمَهَا رَسُولُ اللهِ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) عَلَى ثَمَانِيَةِ أَسْهُمٍ فَالسَّهْمُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْ ثَمَانِيَةٍ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan

text.en: The Imam was asked about a man who bequeathed 'a share' of his estate without saying how much. He said: a share is one of eight; and thus the Messenger of God apportioned the alms into eight shares, so a share is one out of eight.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قوم وحدوا لله ولم تدخل المعرفة في قلوبهم من أن محمداً رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله، فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله يتألفهم ويعلمهم كيما يعرفوا فجعل الله لهم نصيباً في الصدقات لكي يعرفوا ويرغبوا

text.en: The reconciled hearts were a people who professed God's oneness but in whose hearts the knowledge that Muhammad is God's Messenger had not yet settled. The Prophet would win them over and teach them, so God set a share of the alms for them, that they might come to know and be drawn in.

note.en: 'He is an ear' was a jibe that the Prophet believed whatever he was told; the reply grants the word but turns it - he is an ear of good, not of harm [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يصدق الله و يصدق المؤمنين، فإذا شهد عندك المؤمنون فصدقهم. و لا تأتمن شارب الخمر
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz

text.en: God says in His Book, 'He has faith in Allah and trusts the faithful' - meaning he believes God and believes the believers. So when believers testify before you, believe them; and do not entrust your wealth to a wine-drinker.

note.en: To 'oppose' God and His Messenger (yuhadid) means to exceed the bounds God set, in open defiance; its wage is the Fire and lasting disgrace [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إنهم اجتمعوا اثنا عشر فكمنوا لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) في العقبة، و ائتمروا بينهم ليقتلوه، فقال بعضهم لبعض: إن فطن نقول: إنما كنا نخوض و نلعب. و إن لم يفطن لنقتلنه
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Twelve of them gathered and lay in wait for the Messenger of God at the mountain pass, plotting among themselves to kill him. They said to one another: if he notices, we will say we were only chatting and jesting; and if he does not notice, we will kill him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هؤلاء قوم كانوا مؤمنين صادقين ارتابوا وشكوا ونافقوا بعد إيمانهم وكانوا أربعة نفر … واعترف وناب وقال يا رسول الله أهلكني اسمي فسماه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن فقال يا رب اجعلني شهيداً حيث لا يعلم أحد أين أنا فقتل يوم اليمامة ولم يعلم أحد أين قتل فهو الذي عفى الله عنه
narrations.chain: Abu'l-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: These were people who had been sincere believers, then doubted and turned hypocrite after their faith; they were four men. One confessed and repented, saying 'My name has ruined me.' The Prophet renamed him Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman; he asked to be martyred where none would know, fell at Yamama unmarked - he is the one God forgave.

perspectives.en: On who receives the alms, Shia reports place the distribution in the hands of a just imam, who apportions the eight shares to each group according to its need, without excess or stinting [13]. Sunni jurists instead debate whether all eight categories must be covered at all: Ibn Kathir reports that al-Shafi'i and others required covering them, while Malik and much of the early and later community held that the whole may be given to a single category [31].
