sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالآيات - كما ترى - أوضح انطباقاً على حديث العقبة منها على غيره من القصص التي تتضمنها الروايات الأخر الواردة في بيان سبب نزول الآيات

sources.gloss: The verses, as you can see, fit the report of al-Aqaba more clearly than the other stories the various narrations give as the occasion of revelation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ليست الصدقات التي هي زكاة الأموال إلا لهؤلاء

sources.gloss: The charities, which are the zakat on wealth, are for none but these.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في اثني عشر رجلاً وقفوا على العقبة ليفتكوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند رجوعه من تبوك

sources.gloss: It was revealed about twelve men who stood at the mountain pass to kill the Messenger of God on his return from Tabuk.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والمعنى - في الاضافة - مستمع خير لكم وصلاح ومصغ اليه، لا مستمع شر وفساد

sources.gloss: The meaning, on the genitive reading, is: a listener to good and welfare for you, one who heeds it, not a listener to evil and corruption.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: اي يتجاوز حدود الله التي أمر المكلفين ان لا يتجاوزوها، فالمحادة مجاوزة الحد بالمشاقة

sources.gloss: That is, he exceeds the bounds of God that the accountable are commanded not to cross; muhadda is exceeding the bound in defiance.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: والصدقات تتجزى ثمانية أجزاء فيعطى كل إنسان من هذه الثمانية على قدر ما يحتاجون إليه بلا إسراف ولا تقتير يقوم في ذلك الإِمام يعمل بما فيه الصلاح

sources.gloss: The alms are divided into eight portions; each of the eight is given according to their need, without excess or stinting, the imam managing it as best serves them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: هؤلاء قوم كانوا مؤمنين صادقين ارتابوا وشكوا ونافقوا بعد إيمانهم وكانوا أربعة نفر

sources.gloss: These were people who had been sincere believers, then doubted and wavered and turned hypocrite after their faith; they were four men.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يصدق الله و يصدق المؤمنين، فإذا شهد عندك المؤمنون فصدقهم

sources.gloss: He believes God and believes the believers; so when believers testify before you, believe them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إنهم اجتمعوا اثنا عشر فكمنوا لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) في العقبة، و ائتمروا بينهم ليقتلوه

sources.gloss: Twelve of them gathered and lay in wait for the Messenger of God at the mountain pass, plotting among themselves to kill him.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: أحدهما أنه يجب ذلك، وهو قول الشافعي وجماعة. والثاني أنه لا يجب استيعابها، بل يجوز الدفع إلى واحد منها

sources.gloss: One view holds it obligatory to cover them all, the position of al-Shafi'i and a group; the second holds it is not obligatory, and one may give to a single category.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: الْفَقِيرُ الَّذِي لاَ يَسْأَلُ النَّاسَ وَالْمِسْكِينُ أَجْهَدُ مِنْهُ وَالْبَائِسُ أَجْهَدُهُمْ

sources.gloss: The poor man is one who does not ask people; the needy is worse off than he; and the wretched is the worst off of them.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: السَّهْمُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْ ثَمَانِيَةٍ

sources.gloss: A share is one of eight.

essay.en: The passage sets two facing portraits side by side: the hypocrites, men and women, and the faithful, men and women. The hypocrites are all alike, bidding what is wrong, forbidding what is right, and closing their hands - the exact inversion of the believing community. Tabatabai reads these verses against a plot the hypocrites contrived among themselves and a grave deed they intended, which God thwarted so that their scheme came to nothing [1]. Tabrisi glosses their closed hands as withholding their wealth from spending in God's obedience, and reads 'they forgot Allah, so He forgot them' as their abandoning His obedience, so He left them in the Fire and withheld His mercy [2]. Their promised end, shared with the disbelievers, is the Fire forever, God's curse, and a lasting punishment. They are like earlier peoples, stronger and wealthier, who enjoyed their fleeting share and waded into falsehood as those before them did [6]. Tusi treats the roll-call of Noah, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned towns as reproach and warning: God did not wrong them; they wronged themselves [7]. Then the mirror turns. The faithful are comrades of one another, bidding right, forbidding wrong, keeping the prayer, giving the zakat, and obeying God and His Apostle; Tusi notes the verse makes commanding right an obligation on every believer, not a chosen few [8]. Their reward is gardens and eternal dwellings in Eden - and God's pleasure, greater than all of it, is the great success.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك و تعالى لا ينسى و لا يسهو، و إنما ينسى و يسهو المخلوق المحدث … و إنما يجازي من نسيه و نسي لقاء يومه بأن ينسيهم أنفسهم
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Isam al-Kulayni, from Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kulayni, from Ali ibn Muhammad known as Allan, from Abu Hamid Imran ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan ibn Qasim al-Raqqam, from al-Qasim ibn Muslim, from his brother Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim

text.en: God, Blessed and Exalted, does not forget nor grow inattentive; only the created, contingent being forgets and grows inattentive. He requites only the one who forgot Him and forgot the meeting of his Day, by making them forget themselves.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: إنما يعني أنهم نسوا الله في دار الدنيا فلم يعملوا بطاعته فنسيهم في الآخرة، أي لم يجعل لهم في ثوابه شيئا فصاروا منسيين من الجنة
narrations.chain: By his chain, from Abu Ma'mar al-Sa'dani, from Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: It means they forgot God in the abode of this world and did not act in obedience to Him, so He forgot them in the Hereafter - that is, He assigned them no share in His reward, and so they became forgotten from the Garden.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: تأخذون كما أخذت الأمم من قبلكم ذراعا بذراع، و شبرا بشبر، و باعا بباع، حتى لو أن أحدا من أولئك دخل جحر ضب لدخلتموه
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh in al-Amali, from Abu Amr, from Ibn Uqda, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Ma'shar, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet

text.en: You will take up the ways of the nations before you, cubit by cubit, span by span, and arm's length by arm's length, until, were one of them to enter a lizard's hole, you would enter it after them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أولئك قوم لوط، ائتفكت عليهم، أي انقلبت و صار عاليها سافلها
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Those are the people of Lot; their land was overturned upon them - that is, it turned over, and its top became its bottom.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فاحملها، فإن المؤمن محرم للمؤمنة
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh in al-Tahdhib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal

text.en: Convey her, for the believing man is a mahram to the believing woman.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: ألا هل أنبئكم بخير مما أنتم فيه؟ … رضاي عنكم و محبتي لكم خير و أعظم مما أنتم فيه
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Thuwayr, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: Shall I not tell you of something better than what you are in? ... My pleasure with you and My love for you is better and greater than what you are in.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: من سرّه أن يحيى حياتي ويموت مماتي ويسكن جنّتي التي واعدنى الله ربّي جنّات عدن … فليوال علي بن أبي طالب وذرّيّته عليهم السلام من بعده

text.en: Whoever would live my life and die my death and dwell in my Garden that my Lord has promised me, the Gardens of Eden, let him take Ali ibn Abi Talib and his progeny after him as guardians.

perspectives.en: Both traditions describe Eden as the Garden's highest reach and the Prophet's own station. They differ over what opens it. Shia narrations make entry to the very Garden the Prophet was promised conditional on loyalty to Ali and his progeny after him [18]. Ibn Kathir instead names the Prophet's supreme station al-Wasila, the highest rank in the Garden that only one man attains, and describes the promise simply as what God prepared for all who believe, with no such condition [29].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وأنهم تواطئوا على أمر دبروه فيما بينهم فأظهروا عند ذلك كلمة الكفر وهموا على أمر عظيم فحال الله بينهم وبينه فخاب سعيهم ولم يؤثر كيدهم

sources.gloss: They colluded on a matter they contrived among themselves, then uttered the word of disbelief and set their minds on a grave deed; but God came between them and it, so their effort failed and their scheme had no effect.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ويقبضون أيديهم أي يمسكون أموالهم عن إنفاقها في طاعة الله ومرضاته … نسوا الله فنسيهم أي تركوا طاعته فتركهم في النار وترك رحمتهم

sources.gloss: 'They close their hands' means they hold back their wealth from spending in obedience to God and seeking His pleasure ... 'they forgot God, so He forgot them' means they abandoned His obedience, so He left them in the Fire and withheld His mercy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انهم تمتعوا بنصيبهم من الخير العاجل وباعوا بذلك الخير الآجل فهلكوا بشر استبدال … خضتم في الباطل والكذب على الله كالذين تابعوهم على ذلك

sources.gloss: They enjoyed their share of the immediate good and thereby sold away the good of the Hereafter, so they perished by the worst of exchanges ... you waded into falsehood and lying against God, like those who followed them in that.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قوله ألم صورته صورة الاستفهام، والمراد به التقرير والتحذير … لم يكن الله ظالماً لهم بهذا الاهلاك ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

sources.gloss: 'Have they not' has the form of a question, but what is meant by it is affirmation and warning ... God was not unjust to them by this destruction; rather, they were wronging themselves.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على ان الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر من فروض الاعيان لان الله تعالى جعل ذلك من صفات المؤمنين، ولم يخص قوماً دون قوم

sources.gloss: In the verse is a proof that commanding right and forbidding wrong are among the individual obligations, for God made that a quality of the believers and did not single out one group rather than another.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله تبارك و تعالى لا ينسى و لا يسهو، و إنما ينسى و يسهو المخلوق المحدث

sources.gloss: God, Blessed and Exalted, does not forget nor grow inattentive; only the created, contingent being forgets and grows inattentive.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: تأخذون كما أخذت الأمم من قبلكم ذراعا بذراع، و شبرا بشبر، و باعا بباع، حتى لو أن أحدا من أولئك دخل جحر ضب لدخلتموه

sources.gloss: You will take up the ways of the nations before you, cubit by cubit, span by span, and arm's length by arm's length, until, were one of them to enter a lizard's hole, you would enter it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أولئك قوم لوط، ائتفكت عليهم، أي انقلبت و صار عاليها سافلها

sources.gloss: Those are the people of Lot; it was overturned upon them - that is, it turned over, and its top became its bottom.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فاحملها، فإن المؤمن محرم للمؤمنة

sources.gloss: Convey her, for the believing man is a mahram to the believing woman.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: رضاي عنكم و محبتي لكم خير و أعظم مما أنتم فيه

sources.gloss: My pleasure with you and My love for you is better and greater than what you are in.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: من سرّه أن يحيى حياتي ويموت مماتي ويسكن جنّتي التي واعدنى الله ربّي جنّات عدن … فليوال علي بن أبي طالب وذرّيّته عليهم السلام من بعده

sources.gloss: Whoever would live my life and die my death and dwell in my Garden that my Lord has promised me, the Gardens of Eden ... let him take Ali ibn Abi Talib and his progeny after him.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: أعلى منزلة في الجنة مكان يقال له الوسيلة لقربه من العرش، وهو مسكن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الجنة

sources.gloss: The highest station in the Garden is a place called al-Wasila, for its nearness to the Throne, and it is the Prophet's dwelling in the Garden.

essay.en:
The passage opens with a command to the Prophet himself: wage jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be severe with them, for their refuge is hell. Al-Tusi records that the commentators differed over how the hypocrites in particular were to be faced [7].

The next verse exposes them. They swear by Allah that they said nothing, yet they had spoken the word of unfaith and schemed for what they could not reach. Al-Tabrisi records several suggested occasions, among them Abdullah ibn Ubayy's boast that the mightier would expel the abased from Medina [4], while al-Tabatabai reads the sequence as fitting the plot against the Prophet's life on the return from Tabuk [1]. Still, the door stays open: if they repent, it is better for them.

Verses 75 to 77 tell of one who pledged that, were he enriched, he would give charity and live righteously, then begrudged the wealth and turned away; his broken word left hypocrisy settled in his heart until the day he meets his Lord [2]. Al-Tabatabai notes that a broken promise and lying are named here as causes and marks of hypocrisy [2]. Nothing they conceal or whisper escapes God, the knower of the Unseen.

The passage then rebukes those who mock the believers' charity, both the wealthy giver and the poor man who offers only what his effort allows [6]. Al-Tabrisi records the Prophet's word that the best charity is the effort of one who has little [6]. It closes on their ruin: whether the Prophet pleads forgiveness for them or not, even seventy times, Allah will never forgive them, for the seventy stands for abundance, not a fixed number [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: جاهد الكفار و المنافقين بإلزام الفرائض
narrations.chain: his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Wage jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites by binding them to the obligatory duties.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما أقام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله أمير المؤمنين يوم غدير خم كان بحذائه سبعة نفر من المنافقين … فنزل جبرئيل واعلم رسول الله بمقالة القوم فدعاهم وسألهم فأنكروا وحلفوا فأنزل الله { يحلفون بالله ما قالوا } الخ.
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tajir, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Uthman al-Sufi, from Zakariya ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Jafar ibn Muhammad

text.en: When the Messenger of Allah installed the Commander of the Faithful on the Day of Ghadir Khumm, seven of the hypocrites were standing opposite him... Gabriel came down and told the Messenger what they had said; he summoned and questioned them, but they denied it and swore, so Allah revealed, 'They swear by Allah that they did not say it.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هو ثعلبة بن خاطب بن عمرو بن عوف كان محتاجاً فعاهد الله فلما آتاه الله بخل به
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He is Thalaba ibn Hatib ibn Amr ibn Awf. He was in need, so he made a pledge with Allah; but when Allah gave to him, he begrudged it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ذهب علي أمير المؤمنين فآجر نفسه على أن يستقي كل دلو بتمرة يختارها، فجمع تمرا فأتى به النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) و عبد الرحمن بن عوف على الباب، فلمزه- أي وقع فيه- فأنزلت هذه الآية
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, hired himself out to draw water, each bucket for a date of his choosing. He gathered the dates and brought them to the Prophet, while Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was at the door and disparaged him; so this verse was revealed.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: أنّ الله قال لمحمد صلَّى الله عليه وآله وسلم ان تستغفر لهم سبعين مرّة فلن يغفر الله لهم فاستغفِر لهم مأة مرّة ليغفر لهم فأنزل الله { سواء عليهم استغفرت لهم } الآية
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Rida

text.en: Allah said to Muhammad: 'even if you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them.' So he sought forgiveness for them a hundred times, that they might be forgiven; then Allah revealed, 'It is the same for them whether you seek forgiveness for them or not.'

perspectives.en: Both traditions ask how the Prophet was to wage jihad against hypocrites who professed Islam. The Sunni commentators divide over the manner: al-Tabari judges it to be by the sword, as against the idolaters, once a man openly voiced his unbelief [27], while al-Qurtubi records that some restricted it to the tongue and others to the legal penalties, and reads the verse as abrogating every earlier concession of pardon [36]. The Shia commentators, by contrast, hold that the Prophet never fought a hypocrite but won them over, and preserve the Household's reading, 'wage jihad against the disbelievers by means of the hypocrites' [24].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالآيات - كما ترى - أوضح انطباقاً على حديث العقبة منها على غيره من القصص

sources.gloss: So these verses, as you can see, apply more clearly to the report of al-Aqaba than to the other stories.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة أولاً على أن خلف الوعد وكذب الحديث من أسباب النفاق وأماراته.

sources.gloss: The verse indicates, first, that breaking a promise and lying in speech are among the causes and marks of hypocrisy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي ابن سلول حين قال: لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجنَّ الأعزَّ منها الأذل

sources.gloss: And it is said it was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, when he said, 'If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel from it the abased.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل فقيل: يا رسول الله أي الصدقة أفضل قال: جهد المقلّ

sources.gloss: It is related that the Prophet was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best?' He said, 'The effort of one who has little.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واختلفوا في كيفية جهاد الكفار والمنافقين

sources.gloss: They differed over the manner of waging jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وتعليق الاستغفار بالسبعين مرة، والمراد به المبالغة لا العدد المخصوص

sources.gloss: Tying the seeking of forgiveness to seventy times is meant as exaggeration for emphasis, not a specific number.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لما أقام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله أمير المؤمنين يوم غدير خم كان بحذائه سبعة نفر من المنافقين

sources.gloss: When the Messenger of Allah installed the Commander of the Faithful on the Day of Ghadir Khumm, seven of the hypocrites were standing opposite him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: هو ثعلبة بن خاطب بن عمرو بن عوف كان محتاجاً فعاهد الله فلما آتاه الله بخل به

sources.gloss: He is Thalaba ibn Hatib ibn Amr ibn Awf; he was in need, so he made a pledge with Allah, but when Allah gave to him he begrudged it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: جاهد الكفار و المنافقين بإلزام الفرائض

sources.gloss: Wage jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites by binding them to the obligatory duties.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ذهب علي أمير المؤمنين فآجر نفسه على أن يستقي كل دلو بتمرة يختارها

sources.gloss: Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, hired himself out to draw water, each bucket for a date of his choosing.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لم يقاتل منافقاً قطّ إنّما كان يتألّفهم

sources.gloss: He never fought a single hypocrite; he only won them over.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنّ الله قال لمحمد صلَّى الله عليه وآله وسلم ان تستغفر لهم سبعين مرّة فلن يغفر الله لهم فاستغفِر لهم مأة مرّة ليغفر لهم

sources.gloss: Allah said to Muhammad: 'even if you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them'; so he sought forgiveness for them a hundred times, that they might be forgiven.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وأولى الأقوال في تأويل ذلك عندي بالصواب ما قال ابن مسعود، من أن الله أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من جهاد المنافقين، بنحو الذي أمره به من جهاد المشركين

sources.gloss: The soundest of the interpretations, in my view, is that of Ibn Masud: that Allah commanded His Prophet regarding jihad against the hypocrites in the manner He commanded him against the idolaters.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وهذه الآية نسخت كل شيء من العفو والصلح والصفح

sources.gloss: This verse abrogated everything of pardon, reconciliation, and forbearance.

essay.en:
The passage turns from reproaching the hypocrites of Tabuk to the reckoning that awaits them. Those left behind rejoiced at sitting back and told others, 'Do not go forth in this heat.' Tabatabai reads these words as an attempt to discourage the Prophet and undo his effort to rouse people to the campaign [1], while the reply that 'the fire of hell is severer in heat' warns that the discomfort they flee is nothing beside what awaits them. Their brief laughter in this world, the commentators note, will be repaid with long weeping in the next [2].

Should the Prophet return to a faction of them who ask leave to march again, he is told to refuse them forever, since they chose to sit back the first time. Verse 84 then forbids him to pray over any who die or to stand at their graves; Tabrisi observes that this very prohibition shows that standing at a believer's grave to supplicate is a prescribed act of worship, since it would not be singled out for the hypocrite otherwise [3]. Their wealth and children should impress no one: God lets these become a means of punishing them in this world while their souls depart in disbelief [3].

Verse 86 exposes the affluent among them, who seek leave to stay whenever a surah calls to faith and struggle. Tusi explains that the command to 'have faith' bids the believers hold fast and summons the hypocrite to renew his faith and abandon his hypocrisy [10]. They are content to remain 'with those who stay back' - the women and the unfit - and their hearts are sealed [4]. Against them the passage sets the Messenger and those with him, who strive with their wealth and persons; to them belong all the blessings and gardens beneath which rivers flow, the great success that Tusi glosses as a deliverance that lasts forever [13].

note.en: The commentators give the occasion as al-Jadd ibn Qays, who told his people not to march out in the heat, so that God exposed him and his companions [15].

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: و خلف أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) على المدينة، فأرجف المنافقون بعلي (عليه السلام)، فقالوا: ما خلفه إلا تشاؤما به … كذب المنافقون- يا علي- أما ترضى أن تكون أخي و أنا أخاك بمنزلة هارون من موسى، إلا أنه لا نبي بعدي، و أنت خليفتي في امتي، و أنت وزيري و وصيي و أخي في الدنيا و الآخرة

text.en: The Prophet left Ali in charge of Medina, and the hypocrites claimed he did so only out of ill omen. He said: The hypocrites lie, Ali. Are you not content to be to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me, and you are my successor in my community?

note.en: The ban is specific to known hypocrites; Tusi records that the funeral prayer is otherwise a communal duty, offered with five takbirs in Shia practice and four among the other jurists [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: أنّ الله قال لمحمد صلَّى الله عليه وآله وسلم ان تستغفر لهم سبعين مرّة فلن يغفر الله لهم فاستغفِر لهم مأة مرّة ليغفر لهم … وقال { ولا تصلّ على أحد منهم مات أبداً ولا تقم على قبره } فلم يستغفر لهم بعد ذلك ولم يقم على قبر أحد منهم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Rida

text.en: God told Muhammad: were you to ask forgiveness for them seventy times, He would not forgive them; so ask a hundred times that they be forgiven. Then He revealed, 'Never pray over any of them when he dies, nor stand at his graveside,' and afterward he stood at none of their graves.

note.en: Though the words address the Prophet, Tusi notes the warning is meant for the whole community: none should be dazzled by the wealth and children God has given the faithless [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أوصيك بتقوى الله و الورع و الاجتهاد، و اعلم أنه لا ينفع اجتهاد لا ورع فيه، و انظر إلى من هو دونك و لا تنظر إلى من هو فوقك، فكثيرا ما قال الله عز و جل لرسوله (صلى الله عليه و آله): { وَلاَ تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَٰلُهُمْ وَأَوْلَـٰدُهُمْ }
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: He counseled: I enjoin on you fear of God, scrupulousness, and striving; and know that striving with no scrupulousness in it brings no benefit. Look to those beneath you and not to those above you, for often God said to His Messenger, 'Let not their possessions or their children impress you.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: في قوله: { رَضُواْ بِأَن يَكُونُواْ مَعَ ٱلْخَوَالِفِ }. قال: مع النساء
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Asked about God's words, 'They are pleased to be with those who stay back,' Imam al-Baqir said: with the women.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: رغبوا عن اختيار الله واختيار رسول الله وأهل بيته إلى اختيارهم … أم رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ وَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Ala al-Hamadani, raising it, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim

text.en: Imam al-Rida rebuked those who abandon the choice of God, His Messenger, and His Household for a choice of their own, reciting against them, 'Or are they pleased to be with those who stay back, and their hearts have been sealed, so they do not understand?'

perspectives.en: Both traditions read the passage as a rebuke of the Tabuk hypocrites, but they weigh the ban on praying over them differently. Razi ties verse 84 to the Prophet's near-prayer over Abdullah ibn Ubayy and counts the prohibition among the cases where revelation came down in agreement with Umar, calling it a great virtue of his [45]. The Shia narration in al-Safi, from Imam al-Rida, presents the same prohibition as the close of the Prophet's own persistent intercession - he had sought forgiveness for them until God forbade both prayer and standing at their graves - with no such framing [19].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: خاطبوا بذلك غيرهم ليخذلوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ويبطلوا مسعاه في تنفير الناس إلى الغزوة

sources.gloss: They addressed this to others in order to discourage the Prophet and defeat his effort to rouse people to the campaign.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فليضحك هؤلاء المنافقون في الدنيا قليلاً … وليبكوا كثيراً في الآخرة

sources.gloss: Let these hypocrites laugh a little in this world, and let them weep much in the hereafter.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن القيام على القبر للدعاء عبادة مشروعة ولولا ذلك لم يخصَّ سبحانه بالنهي عنه الكافر

sources.gloss: This verse shows that standing at the grave to supplicate is a prescribed act of worship; otherwise God would not have singled out the unbeliever for the prohibition.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف أي رضوا لنفوسهم أن يقعدوا مع النساء والصبيان والمرضى والمقعدين

sources.gloss: 'They are pleased to be with those who stay back' - pleased for themselves to sit with the women, the children, the sick, and the disabled.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والصلاة على الأموات فرض على الكفايات إذا قام به قوم سقط عن الباقين … وفيها خمس تكبيرات عندنا، وعند الفقهاء أربع تكبيرات

sources.gloss: The funeral prayer over the dead is a collective duty; when a group performs it, it drops from the rest, and it has five takbirs according to us and four according to the other jurists.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وبينا أنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله والمراد به الامة، ينهاهم الله أن يعجبوا بما اعطى الله الكفار من الأموال والأولاد في الدنيا

sources.gloss: We explained that it addresses the Prophet but means the community: God forbids them to be impressed by the wealth and children He has given the unbelievers in this world.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهذا خطاب للمؤمنين وأمر لهم بأن يدوموا على الايمان … ويدخل فيه المنافق ويتناوله الأمر بأن يستأنف الايمان ويترك النفاق

sources.gloss: This addresses the believers, commanding them to persist in faith, and it includes the hypocrite, who is commanded to renew his faith and abandon hypocrisy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والفوز النجاة من الهلكة إلى حال النعمة … وإنما وصفه بالعظيم لأنه حاصل على جهة الدوام

sources.gloss: Success is deliverance from destruction to a state of bliss, and it is called great because it is attained everlastingly.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزلت في الجد بن قيس لما قال لقومه: لا تخرجوا في الحر، ففضح الله الجد بن قيس و أصحابه

sources.gloss: It was revealed about al-Jadd ibn Qays, when he told his people, 'Do not go out in the heat'; so God exposed al-Jadd ibn Qays and his companions.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أوصيك بتقوى الله و الورع و الاجتهاد … فكثيرا ما قال الله عز و جل لرسوله (صلى الله عليه و آله): { وَلاَ تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَٰلُهُمْ وَأَوْلَـٰدُهُمْ }

sources.gloss: I enjoin on you fear of God, scrupulousness, and striving; for often God said to His Messenger, 'Let not their possessions or their children impress you.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن جابر، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، في قوله: { رَضُواْ بِأَن يَكُونُواْ مَعَ ٱلْخَوَالِفِ }. قال: مع النساء

sources.gloss: From Jabir, from Imam al-Baqir, regarding 'They are pleased to be with those who stay back': he said, with the women.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وقال { ولا تصلّ على أحد منهم مات أبداً ولا تقم على قبره } فلم يستغفر لهم بعد ذلك ولم يقم على قبر أحد منهم

sources.gloss: And He said, 'Never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave' - so after that he sought no forgiveness for them and stood at none of their graves.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: أن هذا يدل على منقبة عظيمة من مناقب عمر رضي الله عنه، وذلك لأن الوحي نزل على وفق قوله في آيات كثيرة

sources.gloss: This points to a great virtue of Umar, for revelation came down in agreement with his view in many verses.

sources.author: abu abd allah muhammad b. ibrahim al-numani

excerpt.text: رغبوا عن اختيار الله واختيار رسول الله وأهل بيته إلى اختيارهم … أم رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ وَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ

sources.gloss: They turned from the choice of God, His Messenger, and His Household to their own choosing; 'Or are they pleased to be with those who stay back? Their hearts are sealed, so they do not understand.'

essay.en:
These verses close the sura's long reckoning with those who stayed home from the Tabuk campaign, turning now to the desert Arabs around Medina; al-Mizan reads them as continuing the very account that comes before [1]. First come the Bedouins who arrive pleading to be excused. Commentators divide over the word al-mu'adhdhirun: most read it as those who put forward an excuse they did not really have, while others take it as a group who had a genuine excuse [3]. Set against them are the ones who did not even come to explain themselves, who lied to Allah and His Apostle by professing a faith they did not hold [7].

God then clears the genuinely excused. No blame rests on the weak, the sick, or those too poor to equip themselves, so long as they are sincere. Nor is there blame on the men who came asking for a mount and turned away in tears when told none could be found; Majma al-Bayan calls these the weepers [4]. Blame falls only on the well-off who asked leave and were content to stay with those left behind, their hearts sealed. Al-Tibyan explains the seal as a mark the angels can recognize, or as a heart shut so that faith cannot enter it [10].

When the army returns, the hypocrites offer excuses and swear oaths so the believers will let them alone. The Prophet is told not to believe them, to turn from them as filth, and that even the believers' being reconciled to them cannot make God reconciled to them [5]. Finally the sura weighs the Bedouins as a whole. They are harsher in unfaith and, being far from settled life and learning, more apt to be ignorant of the law God revealed; some treat what they spend as a mere fine while they wait for disaster to strike the Muslims [2]. Yet it does not end there. It closes on the believing Bedouin, whose giving God counts as nearness to Him and who is admitted into His mercy.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلا بِدُونِ سَعَتِهِمْ … فَوُضِعَ عَنْهُمْ لانَّهُمْ لا يَجِدُونَ
narrations.chain: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: They were commanded to nothing beyond their capacity. Then, reciting the verse about the weak, the sick, and those who find nothing to spend, he said it was lifted from them because they do not find the means.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: قال مع النساء
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Baqir

text.en: Those left behind, whom the well-off were content to join, are the women.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الغيب: ما لم يكن، و الشهادة: ما قد كان
narrations.chain: Ibn Babuyah, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: About the Knower of the Unseen and the witnessed: the Unseen is what has not yet come to be, and the witnessed is what has already been.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وَيَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنفِقُ قُرُبَاتٍ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ … أ يثيبهم عليه؟ قال: نعم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: He was asked about God's words, that among the Bedouins is one who regards what he spends as a means of nearness to Allah: will He reward them for it? He said, Yes.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات تقبل الاتصال بالآيات التي قبلها وهي تعقب غرضاً يعقبه ما تقدمها.

sources.gloss: The exposition: these verses connect with the ones before them and pursue the same aim as what precedes.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: يبين تعالى حال سكان البادية وأنهم أشد كفراً ونفاقاً لأنهم لبعدهم عن المدنية والحضارة، وحرمانهم من بركات الإنسانية من العالم والأدب أقسى وأجفى

sources.gloss: God describes the state of the desert-dwellers: that they are harsher in unfaith and hypocrisy, because their remoteness from settled civilization and their deprivation of learning and refinement make them harder and coarser.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: المقصّرون الذي يعتذرون وليس لهم عذر عن أكثر المفسرين. وقيل: هم المعتذرون الذين لهم عذر

sources.gloss: According to most exegetes, these are the deficient ones who offer an excuse though they have none; and it is said they were those who did have an excuse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والآية الثانية نزلت في البكائين وهم سبعة نفر

sources.gloss: The second verse was revealed about the weepers, who were seven men.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لا ينفعهم رضاكم عنهم مع سخط الله عليهم وارتفاع رضاه عنهم

sources.gloss: Your being pleased with them does not benefit them while God is angry with them and His good pleasure is withheld from them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يعني المنافقين، لأنهم الذين كذبوا الله ورسوله فيما كانوا يظهرون من الايمان

sources.gloss: That is, the hypocrites, for they are the ones who lied to Allah and His Apostle about the faith they used to display.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وطبع الله على قلوبهم بمعنى وسم قلوبهم بسمة تعرفها الملائكة فيميزون بينهم وبين غيرهم من المؤمنين، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد انه بمنزلة المطبوع في أن لا يدخلها الايمان

sources.gloss: Allah has set a seal on their hearts means He marked their hearts with a sign the angels recognize, distinguishing them from the believers; or it may mean the heart is like something sealed, so that faith cannot enter it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الغيب: ما لم يكن، و الشهادة: ما قد كان

sources.gloss: The Unseen is what has not yet been, and the witnessed is what has already been.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أ يثيبهم عليه؟ قال: نعم

sources.gloss: Will He reward them for it? He said, Yes.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قال مع النساء

sources.gloss: He said: with the women.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: فَوُضِعَ عَنْهُمْ لانَّهُمْ لا يَجِدُونَ

sources.gloss: It was lifted from them because they do not find the means.

title.en: Forerunners and the mosque of harm

essay.en:
The passage turns from the disbelievers and hypocrites of the earlier verses to name the foremost in faith: the early Emigrants and Helpers, and those who followed them in virtue, with whom Allah is pleased. Tabrisi records several views on who these forerunners are - those who prayed toward both qiblas, those who pledged at Hudaybiyya, or the men of Badr - and notes the report that Ali was the first male to believe [3]. Tusi relates that when Umar recited the verse so that only the Emigrants were the forerunners, Ubayy corrected him with a reading that joins their followers through the Commander of the Faithful [8].

Verse 101 warns that hypocrisy has grown hardened among the Bedouins around Madinah and among its townspeople, so settled that the Prophet does not know them though Allah does; they will be punished twice, and Tabrisi lists the proposed pairs - public exposure, the grave, captivity and killing, or the taking of their wealth [4]. As al-Mizan notes, this theme runs through the passage: their disbelief, hypocrisy and faith, with the charity verse set among the verses [1]. Verses 102 to 104 turn to a group who confessed their sins, mixing righteous deeds with evil ones. Qummi ties these verses to Abu Lubaba, who bound himself to a pillar of the mosque until Allah accepted his repentance, then gave a third of his wealth in charity [20]. The command to take a cleansing charity follows, which Tabrisi weighs between an expiation for their sins and the obligatory alms, favoring the latter [5].

Verse 105 bids them work, for Allah, His Apostle and the faithful will see their conduct. Verse 106 leaves a further group suspended for Allah's decree, either punished or forgiven; Tabrisi records that it came down about the three Helpers left behind from Tabuk [6]. The passage closes with the mosque of harm: al-Mizan recounts how a faction built a mosque to harm the mosque of Quba, to divide the believers and to lie in wait for Abu Amir, who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before [2]. The Prophet is forbidden ever to stand in it, and it is set against the mosque founded on Godwariness from the first day; the mosque of harm, by contrast, collapses with its builders into the fire.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Hasan
narrations.arabic: فكما أن للسابقين فضلهم على من بعدهم كذلك لأبي علي بن أبي طالب … فضيلته … على السابقين بسبقه السابقين
narrations.chain: Furat, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Hisham, from Ubada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Mamar Said ibn Khaytham, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Dabbi and Abdallah ibn Sharik al-Amiri, from Sulaym ibn Qays, from al-Hasan ibn Ali

text.en: Just as the vanguard have their merit over those who came after them, so my father Ali ibn Abi Talib has his merit over the vanguard, by outstripping the vanguard themselves.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الذين خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً فأولئك قوم مؤمنون، يحدثون في إيمانهم من الذنوب التي يعيبها المؤمنون و يكرهونها، فأولئك عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from a man, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Those who mixed righteous conduct with other that was evil are a believing people; within their faith they fall into sins that the believers find blameworthy and detest. It is they of whom He says, 'Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: خلطوا عملاً صالحاً وآخر سيئاً عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم والعسى من الله واجب وإِنّما نزلت في شيعتنا المذنبين
narrations.chain: Furat, from Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Fazari, in an unbroken chain, from Khaythama al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar

text.en: They mixed righteous conduct with other that was evil; perhaps Allah will accept their repentance. The 'perhaps' from Allah is binding, and it was revealed about the sinners among our Shia.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألته عن قول الله: خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا جارية هي في الإمام بعد رسول الله … قال: نعم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked him about Allah's words, 'Take charity from their possessions to cleanse them and purify them thereby' - does this remain in force for the Imam after the Messenger? He said, 'Yes.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: المؤمنون ها هنا الأئمة الطاهرون صلوات الله عليهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: In the words 'Allah will see your conduct, and His Apostle and the faithful,' the faithful here are the pure Imams.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: المرجون لأمر الله قوم كانوا مشركين قتلوا حمزة وجعفر وأشباههما من المؤمنين ثم دخلوا بعد ذلك في الإِسلام فوحدوا الله وتركوا الشرك ولم يعرفوا الإِيمان بقلوبهم فيكونوا من المؤمنين فتجب لهم الجنة ولم يكونوا على جحودهم فتجب لهم النار فهم على تلك الحالة مرجون لأمر الله إما يعذبهم وإما يتوب عليهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from Abu al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Those left waiting for Allah's command had been polytheists who killed Hamza, Jafar and their like among the believers, then entered Islam, professing Allah's oneness. They did not grasp faith in their hearts to count as believers due Paradise, nor stayed in denial to be due the Fire; so they remain suspended for Allah's command.

note.en: The 'men who love to keep pure' were understood as those who cleanse themselves with water after relieving themselves, a gloss related from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq [16].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألته عن المسجد الذي أسس على التقوى. فقال: مسجد قبا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked him about the mosque founded on Godwariness. He said, 'The mosque of Quba.'

perspectives.en: The traditions read the vanguard of verse 100 in opposite directions. Sunni commentators take it as a proof about the leading Companions: Ibn Kathir makes the foremost the best of the Companions and warns against anyone who reviles them, naming Abu Bakr above all [53], while al-Razi argues that Abu Bakr, as the first to emigrate, is thereby shown to hold the rightful imamate [72]. The Shia sources center the verse on Ali: Qummi identifies the forerunners as those who stood firm on his wilaya [19], and Furat has Imam al-Hasan place Ali's precedence above the vanguard itself [40].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الكلام جار على الغرض السابق يبين به حال الأعراب في كفرهم ونفاقهم وإيمانهم وفي خلال الآيات آية الصدقة

sources.gloss: The discourse continues the earlier theme, setting out the state of the Bedouins in their disbelief, hypocrisy and faith, with the charity verse falling among these verses.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فكان مسجدهم لمضارَّة مسجد قُبا، وللكفر بالله ورسوله، ولتفريق المؤمنين المجتمعين في قُبا، ولإِرصاد أبي عامر الراهب المحارب لله ورسوله من قبل

sources.gloss: Their mosque was for harming the mosque of Quba, for disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, for splitting the believers who gathered at Quba, and to lie in wait for Abu Amir the monk, who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل: نزلت هذه الآية فيمن صلى إلى القبلتين … وقيل: نزلت فيمن بايع بيعة الرضوان وهي بيعة الحديبية … وقيل: هم أهل بدر … واختلف في أول من أسلم من المهاجرين فقيل: ان أول من آمن خديجة بنت خويلد ثم علي بن أبي طالب

sources.gloss: It is said the verse came down about those who prayed to both qiblas; or about those who gave the pledge of Ridwan at Hudaybiyya; or that they are the people of Badr. There is dispute over who first accepted Islam: some say Khadija first, then Ali ibn Abi Talib.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: سنعذّبهم مرتين فيه أقوال أحدها: أن معناه نعذّبهم في الدنيا بالفضيحة … وقيل: مرة في الدنيا بالسبي والقتل ومرة في الآخرة بعذاب القبر … وقيل: إحداهما أخذ الزكاة منهم والأخرى عذاب القبر

sources.gloss: 'We will punish them twice' has several readings: one, punishment in this world by public exposure and in the grave; another, once in this world by captivity and killing and once in the Hereafter by the punishment of the grave; another, one being the taking of their zakat and the other the punishment of the grave.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وليست بالصدقة المفروضة بل هي على سبيل الكفارة للذنوب التي أصابوها … وقيل: أراد بها الزكاة المفروضة عن الجبائي وأكثر أهل التفسير وهو الظاهر

sources.gloss: Some said it is not the obligatory alms but an expiation for the sins they committed; others - al-Jubbai and most exegetes - held it to mean the obligatory zakat, which is the apparent sense.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال مجاهد وقتادة: نزلت الآية في هلال بن أمية الواقفي ومرارة بن الربيع وكعب بن مالك وهم من الأوس والخزرج

sources.gloss: Mujahid and Qatada said the verse came down about Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn al-Rabi and Kab ibn Malik, who were of the Aws and Khazraj.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وروي أن عمر قرأ { والأنصار } بالرفع { الذين اتبعوهم } باسقاط الواو، فقال أبي: والذين اتبعوهم بأمير المؤمنين فرجعوا إلى قوله

sources.gloss: It is related that Umar recited 'and the Helpers' in the nominative and 'those who followed them' without the connecting waw; Ubayy said, 'and those who followed them through the Commander of the Faithful,' and they went back to his reading.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل: يتطهرون بالماء من الغائط والبول، وهو المروي عن ابي جعفر وابي عبد الله عليهما السلام

sources.gloss: It is said they purify themselves with water from excrement and urine, which is what is related from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهم النقباء أبو ذر والمقداد وسلمان وعمار ومن آمن وصدق وثبت على ولاية أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

sources.gloss: They are the chiefs - Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Salman and Ammar - and whoever believed, held true and stood firm on the wilaya of the Commander of the Faithful.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت في أبي لبابة بن عبد المنذر … ومر إلى المسجد وشد في عنقه حبلاً ثم شده إلى الاسطوانة التي تسمى اسطوانة التوبة وقال لا أحله حتى أموت أو يتوب الله علي … فقال يا رسول الله أفأتصدق بمالي كله؟ قال لا … فبثلثه قال نعم

sources.gloss: It came down about Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir; he went to the mosque, tied a rope around his neck and bound it to the pillar called the pillar of repentance, saying, 'I will not loose it until I die or Allah relents toward me.' He said, 'Messenger of Allah, shall I give away all my wealth in charity?' He said, 'No'; 'A third of it?' He said, 'Yes.'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: المؤمنون ها هنا الأئمة الطاهرون صلوات الله عليهم

sources.gloss: The 'faithful' here are the pure Imams.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: المرجون لأمر الله قوم كانوا مشركين قتلوا حمزة وجعفر وأشباههما من المؤمنين ثم دخلوا بعد ذلك في الإِسلام

sources.gloss: Those left waiting for Allah's command were people who had been polytheists and had killed Hamza, Jafar and their like among the believers, then afterward entered Islam.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الذين خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً فأولئك قوم مؤمنون، يحدثون في إيمانهم من الذنوب التي يعيبها المؤمنون و يكرهونها

sources.gloss: Those who mixed righteous conduct with other that was evil are a believing people; within their faith they fall into sins that the believers find blameworthy and detest.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: سألته عن قول الله: خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا جارية هي في الإمام بعد رسول الله … قال: نعم

sources.gloss: I asked him about Allah's words, 'Take charity from their possessions to cleanse them and purify them thereby' - does it remain in force for the Imam after the Messenger? He said, 'Yes.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: سألته عن المسجد الذي أسس على التقوى. فقال: مسجد قبا

sources.gloss: I asked him about the mosque founded on Godwariness; he said, 'The mosque of Quba.'

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: فكما أن للسابقين فضلهم على من بعدهم كذلك لأبي علي بن أبي طالب … فضيلته … على السابقين بسبقه السابقين

sources.gloss: Just as the vanguard have their merit over those who came after them, so my father Ali ibn Abi Talib has his merit over the vanguard, by his outstripping the vanguard themselves.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: والعسى من الله واجب وإِنّما نزلت في شيعتنا المذنبين

sources.gloss: The 'perhaps' from Allah is binding, and it was revealed about the sinners among our Shia.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فياويل من أبغضهم، أو سبهم … ولا سيما سيد الصحابة بعد الرسول وخيرهم وأفضلهم، أعني الصديق الأكبر … أبا بكر بن أبي قحافة

sources.gloss: Woe to whoever hates them or reviles them, above all the master of the Companions after the Messenger, the best and most excellent of them - namely Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: إن أسبق الناس إلى الهجرة هو أبو بكر … فصارت هذه الآية من أدل الدلائل على فضل أبي بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما، وعلى صحة إمامتهما

sources.gloss: The foremost of people in emigration was Abu Bakr, so this verse became among the clearest proofs of the excellence of Abu Bakr and Umar and of the soundness of their imamate.

title.en: The bargain and those left behind

essay.en: Set between the sura's exposure of the hypocrites and its closing commands, this passage turns to the believers and finishes the account of the Tabuk campaign. It opens with a startling image: God has 'bought from the faithful their souls and their possessions' in exchange for paradise. The commentators read this as a figure of speech, since a buyer purchases what he does not own, whereas God already owns everything; the language of trade is used to seal the certainty of the reward [6]. The bargain is registered 'in the Torah and the Evangel and the Quran,' and the believer is told to rejoice in it. Verse 112 then lists the sellers by their finest traits - penitent, devout, praising God, bowing, prostrating, enjoining right and forbidding wrong, guarding God's bounds - the believers, as al-Mizan puts it, described by their most beautiful attributes [1]. Next comes a hard line: the Prophet and the believers may not plead forgiveness for polytheists, even close kin, once it is clear they belong to the Fire. Occasion reports say Muslims had asked the Prophet to seek pardon for relatives who died in the age of ignorance [3]. Abraham is the test case: his prayer for his father was only to honor a promise, and once his father's enmity to God was plain, he broke with him. Verses 115 and 116 then reassure: God does not fault a people until He has made plain what they must avoid [4], for to Him belongs the kingdom and there is no guardian besides Him. The passage ends by returning to Tabuk: God turned in mercy to the Prophet, the Emigrants, and the Helpers who marched 'in the hour of difficulty' [12], and to the three who were left behind, when the wide earth closed in on them until they knew there was 'no refuge from Allah except in Him.'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: لقي عباد البصري علي بن الحسين (عليه السلام) في طريق مكة، فقال له: يا علي بن الحسين، تركت الجهاد و صعوبته و أقبلت على الحج و لينته … إذا رأينا هؤلاء الذين هذه صفتهم، فالجهاد معهم أفضل من الحج
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Abbad al-Basri met Ali ibn al-Husayn on the road to Mecca and said: you have left jihad and its hardship and turned to the ease of hajj. Ali ibn al-Husayn told him to complete the verse, then said: when we see those who bear this description, jihad alongside them is better than hajj.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما نزلت هذه الآية إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين قام رجل إلى النبيّ صلَّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال يا نبيّ الله أرأيتك الرّجل يأخذ سيفه فيقاتل حتى يقتل إلا أنّه يقترف من هذه المحارم أشهيد هو … فبشّر النبي المجاهدين من المؤمنين الذين هذه صفتهم وحليتهم بالشهادة والجنّة

text.en: When this verse was revealed a man asked the Prophet: if a man fights with his sword until he is killed, yet indulges in some forbidden things, is he a martyr? Then God revealed 'the penitent, the devout,' and the Prophet promised the fighters who bear these traits martyrdom and paradise.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فقال لا إِقْرَأْ التائبين العابدين إلى آخرها فسئل عن العلّة في ذلك فقال اشترى من المؤمنين التّائبين العابدين

text.en: Someone recited the qualities of verse 112 before al-Baqir as a separate phrase. He corrected him: read them joined to the earlier verse - He bought from the believers who are penitent, devout - so the qualities describe the believers whose souls were bought.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله (عليه السلام): ما تقول الناس في قول الله: { وَمَا كَانَ ٱسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لأَبِيهِ إِلاَّ عَن مَّوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ }؟ قلت: يقولون: إن إبراهيم وعد أباه أن يستغفر له؟ قال: ليس هو هكذا، إن إبراهيم وعده أن يسلم فاستغفر له، فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Al-Sadiq asked what people say about 'Abraham's pleading forgiveness for his father was only to fulfill a promise.' I said: they hold Abraham promised his father to seek pardon for him. He said: not so. The father promised he would embrace Islam, so Abraham sought pardon for him; when his enmity to God became plain, Abraham repudiated him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: و في رواية أبي الجارود، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، قال: الأواه: المتضرع إلى الله في صلاته، و إذا خلا في قفرة من الأرض و في الخلوات
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Al-Baqir said: the plaintive one [awwah] is he who humbly entreats God in his prayer, and when he is alone in a barren stretch of land or in secluded places.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قُلْتُ لابِي عَبْدِ الله (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) أَصْلَحَكَ الله هَلْ جُعِلَ فِي النَّاسِ أَدَاةٌ يَنَالُونَ بِهَا الْمَعْرِفَةَ قَالَ فَقَالَ لا قُلْتُ فَهَلْ كُلِّفُوا الْمَعْرِفَةَ قَالَ لا عَلَى الله الْبَيَانُ … قَالَ حَتَّى يُعَرِّفَهُمْ مَا يُرْضِيهِ وَمَا يُسْخِطُهُ
narrations.chain: from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Abd al-A'la asked al-Sadiq: has a faculty been placed in people by which they attain knowledge of God? He said: No. Are they then obliged to know Him? He said: No; the clarification rests with God. Of this verse he said: until He makes them recognize what pleases Him and what angers Him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قوله: { لقد تاب الله بالنبي على المهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة } قال الصادق عليه السلام: هكذا نزلت وهو أبو ذر وأبو خثيمة وعمر بن وهب الذين تخلفوا ثم لحقوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله

text.en: Al-Sadiq said: thus it was revealed - 'God turned in mercy, through the Prophet, to the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of difficulty.' They are Abu Dharr, Abu Khaythama, and Umar ibn Wahb, who lagged behind then caught up with the Messenger of God.

note.en: Ahl al-Bayt read khullifu, left behind, as khalafu, held back in opposition; had they merely been left behind, the commentators note, no blame would fall upon them [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام هم كعب بن مالك ومرارة بن الربيع وهلال بن أميّة

text.en: Al-Sadiq said: they are Ka'b ibn Malik, Mararah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayya.

perspectives.en: On verse 117 the two traditions part over a single word. Shia authorities read 'God turned in mercy through the Prophet (bihi) to the Emigrants and Helpers,' reasoning that the Prophet committed no sin for God to forgive; the clemency reached his community through him [26]. Sunni commentators keep the standard reading, 'God turned to the Prophet (ala al-nabi),' and take his share as the pardon of a minor lapse or a leaving of the more excellent course during the hardship of Tabuk, as al-Razi sets out [53].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: يصف سبحانه المؤمنين بأجمل صفاتهم

sources.gloss: He, Glorified, describes the believers by their most beautiful attributes.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن المسلمين قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا تستغفر لآبائنا الذين ماتوا في الجاهلية فأنزل الله سبحانه هذه الآية

sources.gloss: The Muslims said to the Prophet: will you not seek forgiveness for our fathers who died in the age of ignorance? So God sent down this verse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وما كان الله ليحكم بضلالة قوم بعد ما حكم بهدايتهم حتى يبيّن لهم ما يتقون

sources.gloss: God does not decree a people astray after decreeing their guidance until He makes clear to them what they should guard against.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وحقيقة الاشتراء لا تجوز على الله تعالى، لأن المشتري انما يشتري ما لا يملك، والله تعالى مالك الأشياء كلها

sources.gloss: A real purchase cannot apply to God, for a buyer buys only what he does not own, while God is the owner of all things.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة يعني في الخروج مع إلى تبوك

sources.gloss: 'Who followed him in the hour of difficulty' means in the march out to Tabuk.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي قراءة اهل البيت عليهم السلام { خالفوا } قالوا لأنهم لو خلفوا لما توجه عليهم العتب

sources.gloss: In the reading of the Ahl al-Bayt it is 'khalafu' (they opposed); they said, because had they merely been left behind, no blame would fall upon them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الصادق عليه السلام: هكذا نزلت وهو أبو ذر وأبو خثيمة وعمر بن وهب الذين تخلفوا ثم لحقوا برسول الله

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq said: thus it was revealed - they are Abu Dharr, Abu Khaythama, and Umar ibn Wahb, who lagged behind then caught up with the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إذا رأينا هؤلاء الذين هذه صفتهم، فالجهاد معهم أفضل من الحج

sources.gloss: When we see those who bear this description, jihad alongside them is better than hajj.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن إبراهيم وعده أن يسلم فاستغفر له، فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

sources.gloss: Abraham was promised that his father would embrace Islam, so he sought forgiveness for him; when it became clear he was an enemy of God, he repudiated him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: فبشّر النبي المجاهدين من المؤمنين الذين هذه صفتهم وحليتهم بالشهادة والجنّة

sources.gloss: So the Prophet gave the believing fighters who bear these traits the glad tidings of martyrdom and paradise.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وأيّ ذنب كان لرسُول الله صلَّى الله عليه وآله وسلم حتى تاب الله منه إنّما تاب الله به على أمّته

sources.gloss: What sin did the Messenger of God have that God should turn to him in forgiveness? Rather, God turned in mercy through him to his community.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام هم كعب بن مالك ومرارة بن الربيع وهلال بن أميّة

sources.gloss: al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq: they are Ka'b ibn Malik, Mararah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayya.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: صدر عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام شيء من باب ترك الأفضل، وهو المشار إليه بقوله تعالى: { عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ }

sources.gloss: Something in the category of leaving the more excellent course issued from the Prophet, alluded to in God's words, 'May God pardon you! Why did you give them leave?'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: قَالَ حَتَّى يُعَرِّفَهُمْ مَا يُرْضِيهِ وَمَا يُسْخِطُهُ

sources.gloss: He said: until He makes them recognize what pleases Him and what angers Him.

essay.en: al-Mizan places these verses within the surah's treatment of fighting [1]. The passage opens with a command that stands over the retreat the surah has just condemned: 'Be wary of Allah, and be with the Truthful.' Tabrisi records several readings of 'the Truthful,' from those honest in word and deed to a report from al-Baqir that names the family of Muhammad [2]; Tusi records the same range, including the reading that ties the word to the men of Al-Ahzab 23, Hamza, Jafar and Ali [5]. The next two verses return to the march on Tabuk. Tabrisi reads 'It is not fitting for the people of Madinah' as a reproach of those who hung back once God had accepted the others' repentance [3], and the verses promise that no thirst, fatigue, hunger, or valley crossed in God's way goes unwritten as a righteous deed. The last verse sets a limit on the summons. Not all the faithful are to march out at once; Tusi records the view that this abrogates the earlier general call, since fighting is a communal duty and not an individual one [6]. Instead a group from each section should go forth to become learned in religion and warn their people on return. Fayd Kashani gathers reports that read this of seeking knowledge and carrying it home [17], and the passage closes by turning the duty of the sword into a duty of learning.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إيانا عنى
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mualla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Ahmad ibn Aidh, from Ibn Udhayna, from Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli

text.en: I asked Abu Jafar about God's words 'and be with the Truthful.' He said: He meant us.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: الصادقون: هم الأئمة الصديقون بطاعتهم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: The Truthful are the Imams, the truthful ones by their obedience.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: أما المؤمنون فعامة لأن جماعة المؤمنين أمروا بذلك، و أما الصادقون فخاصة لأخي علي و الأوصياء من بعده إلى يوم القيامة

text.en: As for the believers, it is general, for all the believers were commanded by it; but as for the Truthful, it is specific to my brother Ali and the successors after him until the Day of Resurrection.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هم في عذر ما داموا في الطلب، و هؤلاء الذين ينتظرونهم في عذر حتى يرجع إليهم أصحابهم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb

text.en: Asked what people should do if something befalls the Imam, he replied: they are excused as long as they are searching, and those who wait for them are excused until their companions return to them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: تفقّهوا في الدين فانّه من لم يتفقّه منكم في الدين فهو اعرابي

text.en: Become learned in religion, for whoever among you does not become learned in religion is a bedouin.

perspectives.en: Verse 119 divides the traditions. Shia narrations read 'the Truthful' as a designation of persons: al-Baqir and al-Rida gloss it as the Imams, and a report has the Prophet tell Salman the word is specific to Ali and his successors [13]. Tabari reads it more broadly and relays views that gloss it as being with the Prophet and his companions, or with Abu Bakr and Umar [19]. Al-Razi, himself Sunni, presses the wording further, arguing that the fallible must be with one immune from error in every age, so that an infallible guide is always present [30].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان آيات في أغراض متفرقة يجمعها غرض واحد مرتبط بغرض الآيات السابقة فإنها تتكلم حول القتال

sources.gloss: An exposition of verses on various aims united by one aim linked to the aim of the preceding verses, for they speak around fighting.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروى جابر عن أبي جعفر ع في قوله { وكونوا مع الصادقين } قال مع آل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: Jabir reported from Abu Jafar (al-Baqir), concerning 'and be with the Truthful,' that he said: with the family of Muhammad.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ذكر عقيب ذلك على وجه التوبيخ لهم والإزراء على ما كانوا فعلوه فقال { ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله }

sources.gloss: He mentioned this afterward by way of reproaching them and censuring what they had done, saying: It is not for the people of Madinah and the bedouins around them to hang back behind the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إن المراد بالصادقين هم الذين ذكرهم الله في قوله { رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه فمنهم من قضى نحبه } وهم حمزة وجعفر { ومنهم من ينتظر } يعني علياً عليه السلام

sources.gloss: It is said the Truthful are those God named in 'men who were true to their covenant with God': Hamza and Jafar, and 'among them is he who awaits,' meaning Ali.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال ابن زيد: هذا حين كان المسلمون قليلين، فلما كثروا نسخ بقوله { وما كان المؤمنين لينفروا كافة فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة } وهذا هو الأقوى لأنه لا خلاف ان الجهاد من فروض الكفايات

sources.gloss: Ibn Zayd said: this was when the Muslims were few; when they grew many it was abrogated by 'It is not for the faithful to go forth en masse.' This is the strongest view, for there is no dispute that jihad is a communal obligation.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الصادقون: هم الأئمة الصديقون بطاعتهم

sources.gloss: The Truthful are the Imams, the truthful ones by their obedience.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هم في عذر ما داموا في الطلب، و هؤلاء الذين ينتظرونهم في عذر حتى يرجع إليهم أصحابهم

sources.gloss: They are excused as long as they are searching, and those who wait for them are excused until their companions return to them.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: تفقّهوا في الدين فانّه من لم يتفقّه منكم في الدين فهو اعرابي

sources.gloss: Become learned in religion, for whoever among you does not become learned in religion is a bedouin.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن الضحاك، في قوله: { وكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ } قال: مع أبي بكر وعمر وأصحابهما رحمة الله عليهم

sources.gloss: From al-Dahhak, concerning 'and be with the Truthful,' he said: with Abu Bakr and Umar and their companions.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فهذا يدل على أنه واجب على جائز الخطأ كونه مع المعصوم عن الخطأ حتى يكون المعصوم عن الخطأ مانعاً لجائز الخطأ عن الخطأ، وهذا المعنى قائم في جميع الأزمان، فوجب حصوله في كل الأزمان

sources.gloss: This indicates that it is obligatory upon the one liable to error to be with the one immune from error, so that the infallible keeps the fallible from error; and this meaning holds in every age, so it must obtain in every age.

essay.en:
These verses close the surah with a command: fight the disbelievers nearest to you, and let them find severity in you. Al-Tusi reads this as a standing duty on the people of every frontier to defend themselves, starting with the closest enemy [5]. Al-Tabatabai groups the surah's closing verses as varied concerns bound to fighting in God's way [1].

The passage then sorts the community by how each side meets a new surah. When one comes down, some ask mockingly whose faith it increased; in the believers it does increase, and they rejoice, while the sick-hearted only add defilement to defilement and die as disbelievers. Al-Qummi reads this as a refutation of those who claim faith neither rises nor falls [13], and Al-Tabatabai treats the mocking question itself as a mark of hypocrisy [2]. They are tried once or twice a year yet neither repent nor take heed; Al-Qummi glosses the trial as illness [14]. When a surah comes they glance around to see if anyone is watching, then slip away, and God turns their hearts aside because they chose falsehood over truth [15].

The surah ends with the Messenger himself: he has come from among the people, pained by their hardship, full of care for the faithful. Al-Tabrisi records a variant reading that renders the phrase 'the noblest among you,' and notes it is said to be the reading of Fatimah [4]. Al-Tusi records that verse 129 was the last of the Quran to be revealed [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عن عمران بن عبد الله القمي، عن جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام) في قول الله تبارك و تعالى: { قَاتِلُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْكُفَّارِ } ، قال: " الديلم "
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Imran ibn Abdillah al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad

text.en: Regarding God's words 'Fight the faithless who are in your vicinity,' he said: the Daylam.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قُلْتُ قَدْ فَهِمْتُ نُقْصَانَ الإيمَانِ وَتَمَامَهُ فَمِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَتْ زِيَادَتُهُ فَقَالَ قَوْلُ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَإِذا ما أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزادَتْهُمْ إِيماناً وَهُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ … وَلَكِنْ بِتَمَامِ الإيمَانِ دَخَلَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْجَنَّةَ وَبِالزِّيَادَةِ فِي الإيمَانِ تَفَاضَلَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِالدَّرَجَاتِ عِنْدَ الله وَبِالنُّقْصَانِ دَخَلَ الْمُفَرِّطُونَ النَّارَ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Abu Amr al-Zubayri, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: He was asked where the increase of faith comes from. He answered with God's words, 'Whenever a surah is sent down, some say: Which of you did it increase in faith?' Had faith been one thing with no increase or decrease, none would excel another; by increase in faith believers rise in degrees.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عن إسحاق بن عمار، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، قال: " هكذا أنزل الله عز و جل: لقد جاءنا رسول من أنفسنا عزيز عليه ما عنتنا حريص علينا بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم "
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Thus God revealed it: 'There has certainly come to us a messenger from among ourselves; grievous to him is our distress; he has deep concern for us, and is most kind and merciful to the faithful.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: تلا هذه الآية { لَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ } ، قال: " من أنفسنا " … " بشيعتنا رءوف رحيم، فلنا ثلاثة أرباعها، و لشيعتنا ربعها "
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: He recited the verse 'a messenger from among yourselves' and said: from among ourselves … to our Shia He is kind and merciful; three quarters are ours, and a quarter for our Shia.

perspectives.en: On 'a messenger from among yourselves,' the traditions diverge. Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir take the phrase to mean the Prophet is of the Arabs' own kind, sharing their language and descent, and cite his birth from lawful marriage rather than fornication [27][32]. The Shia narrations in al-Burhan instead preserve the reading 'from among ourselves,' referring to the Ahl al-Bayt, and apportion the verse's four descriptions so that three belong to them and 'kind and merciful to the believers' is shared with their Shia [20].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان آيات في أغراض متفرقة يجمعها غرض واحد مرتبط بغرض الآيات السابقة فإنها تتكلم حول القتال

sources.gloss: An exposition of verses with scattered aims gathered under one aim tied to that of the previous verses, for they speak about fighting.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: يتحصل بذلك أيضاً أمارة من أمارات النفاق يعرف بها المنافق من المؤمن، وهو قولهم عند نزول القرآن أيّكم زادته هذه إيماناً

sources.gloss: By this too a mark of hypocrisy emerges, by which the hypocrite is known from the believer: their saying, when the Quran comes down, 'Which of you did this increase in faith?'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ ابن عباس وابن علية وابن محيصن والزهري من أنفَسِكم بفتح الفاء. وقيل: إنها قراءة فاطمة … ومن قرأ { من أنفسِكم } بفتح الفاء فمعناه من أشرفكم ومن خياركم

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas and others read 'min anfasikum' with a fatha, and it is said to be Fatimah's reading … whoever reads 'min anfasikum' with a fatha, its meaning is 'from the noblest and best of you.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يجب على اهل كل ثغر أن يقاتلوا دفاعاً عن أنفسهم اذا خافوا على بيضة الاسلام إذا لم يكن هناك إمام عادل

sources.gloss: The people of every frontier must fight in defense of themselves when they fear for the heartland of Islam, if there is no just imam present.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال ابي بن كعب وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وقتادة: هذه آخر آية نزلت من القرآن ولم ينزل بعدها شيء

sources.gloss: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: this is the last verse of the Quran revealed, and nothing was revealed after it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهو رد علي من يزعم أن الإِيمان لا يزيد ولا ينقص

sources.gloss: It is a refutation of whoever claims that faith neither increases nor decreases.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أو لا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين } أي: يمرضون

sources.gloss: 'Do they not see that they are tried once or twice every year' means: they fall ill.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قلوبهم } عن الحق إلى الباطل باختيارهم الباطل على الحق

sources.gloss: Their hearts turned from truth to falsehood, because they chose falsehood over truth.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن عمران بن عبد الله القمي، عن جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام) في قول الله تبارك و تعالى: { قَاتِلُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْكُفَّارِ } ، قال: " الديلم "

sources.gloss: From Imran ibn Abdillah al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on 'Fight the faithless who are in your vicinity': the Daylam.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن إسحاق بن عمار، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، قال: " هكذا أنزل الله عز و جل: لقد جاءنا رسول من أنفسنا عزيز عليه ما عنتنا حريص علينا بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم "

sources.gloss: From Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah: 'Thus God revealed it: There has certainly come to us a messenger from among ourselves, grievous to him is our distress, full of concern for us, kind and merciful to the believers.'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: مِنْ أنْفُسِكُمْ } تعرفونه لا من غيركم … لم يصبه شيء من شرك في ولادته

sources.gloss: 'From yourselves' - you know him, not from anyone else … nothing of idolatry touched him in his birth.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: أرسل إليهم رسولاً من أنفسهم، أي من جنسهم، وعلى لغتهم

sources.gloss: He sent them a messenger from among themselves, that is, of their own kind and in their language.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: قُلْتُ قَدْ فَهِمْتُ نُقْصَانَ الإيمَانِ وَتَمَامَهُ فَمِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَتْ زِيَادَتُهُ فَقَالَ قَوْلُ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَإِذا ما أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزادَتْهُمْ إِيماناً وَهُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ

sources.gloss: I said: I have understood the decrease and completion of faith; from where does its increase come? He said: the words of Allah, 'Whenever a surah is sent down, some say, Which of you did this increase in faith? As for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice.'
